items.statement: Digital collections at >80% of total collections; cash collections <20%
items.quote: Today, we collect more than 80% through digital route and less than 20% is thr ough cash collection mode

items.statement: Insurance income via corporate agency at INR7.52 crores classified as other income; expected to increase further
items.quote: The other income, which has significantly increased over quarter 1 to quarter 4, and then we are also planning that this income is going to further increase in this financial year, is an insurance income that -- through corporate agency, we have taken a INR7.52 crores that has been classified as other income in my

items.statement: Conscious decision to stop co-lending business (was INR900+ crores, now INR595 crores) due to partner stress; co-lending portfolio was 0 NPA but degrowing; focusing on own MCSL portfolio growth
items.quote: But by that time, we built our own team and we built capability for doing our own business. And with the fact that we saw some stress in co-lending partners, with our partners, as Raman has already said that one account has gone NPA, we took a conscious decision to stop the co-lending business as a whole, okay?

items.statement: Not entering new geographies this year; going deeper in existing markets (Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu) and calibrated growth in North; incremental portfolio NPA well below peer group per credit bureau dashboard
items.quote: Therefore, we are not entering into any new geographies this year. We are only going deeper in the places where we are already present. So those are the checks and balances that we are keeping in mind.

items.statement: 2-wheeler credit team to reduce from 30 to 3-4 people due to automation; disbursement operations team to reduce from 45 to 5 people with AI tool reaching 90% STP
items.quote: So the last leg was -- so once the risk -- credit underwriting becomes automated, we had about 30-odd people doing 2-wheeler credit, okay? That team will now get reduced to 3 or 4 because they just need to monitor the BREs.

items.statement: ARC security receipts reduced: Phoenix ARC from INR103 crores to INR26 crores; second ARC from INR41 crores to INR23 crores; legacy risk largely behind
items.quote: The SR at the start of the financial year -- sorry, at the start of the ARC was INR103 crores. Now that has been brought down to INR26 crores with business in my Phoenix ARC. And then similarly, another ARC that we did, which was at the start of this financial year, which was around INR41 crores. So INR23 crores was the closing outstanding from those SRs.

items.statement: Pre-COVID doubtful portfolio (INR12 crores) written off with P&L hit; 8 fraud loan accounts (INR43.15 lakhs) fully provided; new wage code impact INR1.68 crores for gratuity/leave encashment
items.quote: The company has taken a call on the portfolio, which was sourced pre-COVID, and that was lying in the doubtful 2 and doubtful 3 category. So around INR12 crores of the portfolio has been taken out from the books wherein we have taken -- for the entire portfolio, we have taken the P&L hit as well.

items.statement: IPO pipeline for FY27: over 250 active applications to raise Rs. 1.75 lakh crores
items.quote: As we enter FY27, the IPO pipeline remains robust, with more than 250 active applications to raise Rs. 1.75 lakh crores, reinforcing our position as a leading global fundraising venue.

items.statement: SGF contribution rate reduced from 5% to 3.5% of profits as threshold of 150% coverage crossed
items.quote: We have crossed it, and in that situation, we are reducing the contribution requirement per quarter from 5% to 3.5%.

items.statement: Target to increase broker count to at least 700 on derivatives platform

items.statement: Target to grow FPI count to around 800 from current 520

items.statement: Target FPI participation in BSE volumes to reach around 9% from current 5-6%

items.statement: Domestic institutional investors deployed close to Rs. 8.5 lakh crores in FY26, a sharp step-up over previous years
items.quote: Domestic institutional investors, including mutual funds, insurance companies, banks and other long-term pools of capital, deployed close to Rs. 8.5 lakh crores during FY26, representing a sharp step-up over previous years.

items.statement: Retail SIP flows reached a record Rs. 3.5 lakh crores in FY26
items.quote: Equally encouraging has been the continued commitment of India's retail investors, whose SIP flows reached a record Rs. 3.5 lakh crores for the year.

items.statement: BSE added 3.53 crore new investor accounts in FY26, total registered accounts cross 25 crore
items.quote: Over the past year alone, BSE has added 3.53 crores new investor accounts, with 10 states each contributing more than 1 crore registered investors, underscoring the broad-based expansion of India's capital markets across regional demographics.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA more than doubled to Rs. 3,079 crores with margins expanding to 64% from 51% in FY26
items.quote: The operating EBITDA, including contribution to core SGF, has more than doubled to Rs. 3,079 crores as compared to Rs. 1,500 crores, with margins expanding to 64% from 51%.

items.statement: Net profit grew 88% to Rs. 2,497 crores with profit margins expanding to 49% from 41%
items.quote: The net profit attributable to the shareholders of the company has demonstrated a significant acceleration to reach Rs. 2,497 crores from Rs. 1,326 crores, representing a robust year-on-year growth of 88%. The profit margins have expanded to 49% from 41%.

items.statement: BSE ranked first globally for IPO listings in FY26 with 255 new listings raising Rs. 1.8 lakh crores, highest ever in number and funds mobilized
items.quote: The BSE IPO market was 4 BSE - PUBLIC ranked first globally for IPO listings in FY2026, welcoming 255 new listings across main board and SME markets and raising a total of Rs. 1.8 lakh crores. This represents a continuation of the strong momentum seen in recent years, but FY26 stands out as the highest ever, both in terms of number of issues and funds mobilized

items.statement: Business fundraising platforms enabled issues to raise Rs. 26.9 lakh crores in FY26 via equity, debt, bonds, CPs, REITs, InvITs, municipal bonds
items.quote: Overall, business fundraising platforms remain the preferred choice by Indian companies to raise capital by enabling issues to raise Rs. 26.9 lakh crores in FY26 by means of equity, debt, bonds, commercial papers, REITs, INVITs, and municipal bonds.

items.statement: BSE StAR MF revenues grew 24% YoY to Rs. 285 crores; total transactions up 27% to 84 crores; monthly peak of 8.2 crore transactions in March 2026

items.statement: Index derivatives average daily premium turnover reached record Rs. 19,523 crores in FY26, up 118% YoY from Rs. 8,978 crores
items.quote: The BSE index derivatives segment continued to demonstrate strong momentum in FY26, with average daily premium turnover reaching a record of Rs. 19,523 crores compared to Rs. 8,978 crores in FY25, translating into a robust year-on-year growth of approximately 118%.

items.statement: Cash market ADTV hit highest ever at Rs. 7,950 crores in FY26
items.quote: FY26 marked a milestone with BSE recording its highest ever ADTV of Rs. 7,950 crores.

items.statement: Co-location revenues increased to Rs. 171 crores in FY26 from Rs. 74 crores in FY25, reflecting strong growth and healthy utilization
items.quote: For FY26, co-location revenues increased to Rs. 171 crores compared to Rs. 74 crores in FY25, reflecting strong growth, healthy utilization levels and the continued benefit of the revised Throttle Charges Framework introduced in July 2025.

items.statement: Monthly contract volumes grew 5x, index futures volumes grew 3x (on smaller base); Bankex showing traction in monthly contracts
items.quote: Monthly contract volumes have gone up by 5x. Index futures have gone up by 3x. Of course, they are all on a smaller base. That is what we are keeping track of and we are working for, and we will continue to work to deepen it in this fashion.

items.statement: Approvals received for three new monthly index derivatives: BSE Focused IT, Focused MidCap, Sensex Next 30; Focused IT derivatives launching 11 May 2026
items.quote: BSE has received approvals for three new monthly index derivatives – BSE Focused IT, Focused MidCap, and Sensex Next 30. items.statement: Launched StAR NPS platform on April 22, 2026 to capture full financial lifecycle from first SIP to final pension
items.quote: BSE Technologies launched StAR NPS on April 22, 2026. This platform aims to simplify and streamline retirement planning for millions of Indians by providing a unified architecture for the national pension system.

items.statement: Broker count on derivatives platform increased from 446 to 587; FPI count grew from 100 to 520; co-location racks increased from 300 to 500
items.quote: As you would know, in the last one year, the member count has increased from 446 to 587. FP Is have increased from 100 to 520. Colo-racks have increased from 300 to 500.

items.statement: Department of Post onboarded as member on BSE StAR MF in January 2026; Dak Sevaks executed over 1,500 transactions
items.quote: I am happy to update that the StAR MF has become the first platform to go live for Dak Sevaks who have executed over 1,500 transactions till date.

items.statement: No intention to reduce IPF or statutory contributions; option pricing reviewed based on internal estimates, not external factors
items.quote: Contributions to IPF and other statutory things are governed by SEBI rules, so there will be no intention to reduce any of them, and we will continue to be supporting all those noble causes stipulated by the regulators in the normal fashion as what we have been doing all along.

items.quote: In the last two years, we have built around Rs. 500 crores as gross block, which has gone for capacity increase. items.quote: If you may recall, since we are not able to project what will be the future SGF, because it is based on a complex set of parameters, we had initially decided that as BSE, in order to prevent any sudden jerks in the P&L, we will voluntarily contribute a specified stipulated percentage of our profits into SGF every quarter, and we put a threshold of maximum up to which we will contribute.

items.statement: India branded business expected to grow at double-digit or low-teens; overall India growth may be lower due to trade generics rationalization for next few quarters

items.quote: International business single -digit growth should continue potentially from Q1 but more likely from Q2.

items.quote: On a 12 -month basis, I would say that it would be having a positive momentum. There are a sufficient number of new projects and new contracts on hand.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to ~70% from 66% YoY; adjusted EBITDA margin ~27% vs 25% YoY; improvement driven by trade generics exit and product mix
items.quote: Gross margin improved to around 70% from 66% compared to the corresponding quarter of previous year. Adjusted EBITDA margin was about 27% compared to 25% in the corresponding quarter of previous year, an improvement of approximately 2%.

items.quote: I would like to wait for one more quarter. First quarter will be indicative of where we are headed for.

items.quote: Without the trade generics business, if we look at the branded business of JB for the India portfolio, that grew at 8% for the quarter. In FY '26, the India business grew 9% to INR2,461 crores and out of this, the branded business grew 11%.

items.quote: Consequently, the International formulations business for the quarter reported a de -growth of 9% to INR259 crores. For FY '26, international formulations revenue grew 2% year -on-year to INR1,154 crores.

items.statement: Trade generics business (~7-8% of India sales till Q3) discontinued; focus shifted entirely to branded business growth
items.quote: The trade generics contribution to the overall India top line is about 7 % to 8% or was about 7% to 8% till Q3, which we've taken steps to significantly rationalize.

items.quote: We believe is more likely and in fact quite likely from the chronic business with the large chronic and especially the cardiac brands where definitely the coverage gap between JB and Torrent is an opportunity.

items.statement: CDMO has top 5 global OTC companies (Innova, Kenvue, P&G, Reckitt) as customers; strategy to increase wallet share and geographic footprint
items.quote: We have, you know, the top companies in the world in the customer mix. So, there's companies like Innova, Kenvue, P&G, Reckitt, these are all part of JB's customer mix.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance; CDMO capacity exists but execution bottlenecks in product development need more resources
items.quote: JB had a very lean development organization, product development and so we need to bring additional resources to product development so that the projects can be kind of executed faster.

items.statement: CDMO capacity available; challenge is execution speed of signed contracts, not capacity
items.quote: Customers are there, capacities are there, it is just the execution that needs to be addressed.

items.statement: Alignment of trade and sales closing practices with Torrent including credit period, field incentives, and cut-off policies done in Q4
items.quote: Alignment of trade and sales closing practices with the parent entity including credit period, field incentives, and cut -off policies.

items.statement: Net cash position ~INR1,200 cr as of FY26 end
items.quote: Rahul, it is around INR1,200 cr.

items.statement: Merger of JB Pharma with Torrent in final stage; hearing in second week of June; expected effective in 1-2 months
items.quote: the last phase of the merger process and the hearing date which we've got is in the second week of June. So, let's see. Devansh Jain: Any tentative timeline around it or? Sudhir Menon: So, I think it should be one to two months' time max for the merger should get effective I would say

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR9.3 per equity share (face value INR1) for FY26
items.quote: The Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of INR9.3 per equity share of INR1 each for the year FY'26.

items.statement: International attrition minimal; distributor-led model; only Russia has overlap with Torrent requiring rationalization
items.quote: No Alok, the attrition there has been minimal. So, basically JB has a distributor led model, right, with direct subsidiaries only in two countries, South Africa where there is zero overlap with Torrent and Russia where there is some overlap.

items.statement: Procurement synergies with Torrent started showing positive impact from April 2026; full impact may be muted by geopolitics
items.quote: Second would be procurement synergies which will start playing out now, but of course in the current year given the external geopolitics, the full impact of those synergies may not be visible, but certainly we are seeing a strong positive impact already from April.

items.statement: Corporate overhead cost synergies from distribution network optimization and back-end function consolidation expected
items.quote: Third would be in the corporate overhead costs which things like distribution network optimization which has already been done and should start taking effect from April in terms of visibility in margin improvement. items.statement: West Asia shipping disruptions (container constraints) create uncertainty for International business in Q1; Asia/Southeast Asia recovering
items.quote: West Asia is anybody's guess. So all in all, we think, you know, Q1 is a little bit uncertain but Q2 onwards we should be on track.

items.statement: CDMO execution risk: lean product development organization causing delays in delivering signed contracts
items.quote: JB has some delays in execution of these contracts which are on hand. So our job is to accelerate the delivery of these new products so that they can come into our revenue quicker rather than later.

items.statement: India business market share growth: 11% vs IPM 10% per IQVIA MAT March 2026; chronic 19% vs industry 14%
items.quote: As per the IQVIA MAT March '26 data set, the India business grew at 11% versus the IPM growth of 10%. The chronic business grew at 19% versus the industry growth of 14%.

items.statement: Revenue INR904 cr in Q4 FY26 (-5% YoY); adjusted EBITDA flat at INR241 cr; adjusted PAT INR150 cr; one-offs INR40 cr (non-cash ESOP)
items.quote: The company recorded revenue of INR904 crores, registering a de -growth of 5%. During the quarter, the one -offs including non -cash ESOP charges amounted to INR40 crores. Adjusted for such one -offs, EBITDA is flat at INR241 crores.

items.statement: Management expects to outgrow the steel market by 1-3% annually on average over a cycle, not the 10-12% seen in recent years.
items.quote: If you want to model long-term the Vesuvius model, the reasonable but solid assumption is that we outgrow the market on average over a cycle, whatever we call a cycle, by between 1% and 3%.

items.statement: Capex run rate of ~650-700 Cr over last 3 years may continue or exceed; investment is outcome-based, not target-driven.
items.quote: We do not invest for the sake of investing. I think that Mohinder mentioned that. We invest to follow the market growth. So we do not say, we want to invest 300 Crores or 600 Crores. We study the

items.statement: Kolkata VISO plant expansion approved; significant capacity addition at marginal cost, commissioning in 12-18 months once triggered.
items.quote: The investment is defined. It is already approved. The only question is, when do we push the button? And we push the button depending on our survey of the demand, and once we push a button, it takes place between 12 and 18 months for this to be on stream

items.statement: Vizag complex at ~1/3 land utilization; 42 acres allow major brownfield expansion for AlSi mono, basic mono, plastics, tap hole clay.
items.quote: it is only used at one third of the space that we have. So the potential for expansion for the AlSi mono or basic mono plant, I am eagerly waiting for Mohinder to tell the bo ard. I do not have enough capacity, I need more

items.statement: AlSi monolithic line (120k tonnes) commissioned Nov 2024, ramped May-Jun 2025; headroom for next couple of years.
items.quote: That line was commissioned in November 2024. I mean it really started kicking in in May, June 2025. We are and you know it is a learning experience to make that to make to make that line dance and we are on our way to making sure that that line works super efficiently and delivers its maximum performance.

items.statement: Plastic refractory plant operational at Vizag; niche market estimated 10k-20k tonnes, used in reheating furnaces and power plant boilers.
items.quote: We are not talking of tens of thousands of tons here. If I was to make an educated guess, somewhere between 10,000 to 20,000 tons.

items.statement: Healthy order book for BOF and EAF furnace lining bricks; entered segment in last year, now established player.
items.quote: We are today very happy to say, we are an established player in basic oxygen furnace lining, electric arc furnace lining. So that was one, that was a big gap that we have filled in the last, I would say not even two years, I would say in the last one year. We have a very healthy order book on that side.

items.statement: New products (last 5 years) represent 20-25% of sales globally and in India; key KPI for management.
items.quote: As Mohinder said at the beginning about new product sales, which are representing typically 20% to 25% of the sales which are products developed in the last five years, and this percentage is not only in India, it is worldwide.

items.statement: Vesuvius maintains 50-55% market share in flow control; technological edge widening due to 2x R&D spend vs nearest competitor.
items.quote: We continue to sell at a higher price than our competitors, and our market share remains above the 50%-55%, and this does not change. And we do not see that changing in the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Competitors may offer deep discounts ("Christmas sales") but customers return due to lower failure rates (99.9999% vs 98%) and better P&L impact.
items.quote: Our products, they do not perform well 98% of the time, they perform well 99.9999% of the time. And this is where the financial difference for the customer lies. Because where the customer loses money is when they have an incident.

items.statement: Pricing power limited; customers consolidate buying (JSW, Tata). Premium maintained via service, quality consistency, reliability, not price competition.
items.quote: Pricing is determined totally by customers nowadays. Customers today are all consolidated. We look at all the big players. They have five, six players. steel plants within themselves. Take JSW. One man negotiates for at least four or five steel plants from the sam e group

items.statement: Raw material cost pressure (alumina spike Jan 2025, war-driven); mitigated by systematic alternate supplier trials (3-9 months) and group-level procurement leverage.
items.quote: Raw materials January 2025 was a crazy period. Aluminas went through the roof. Again, we are in the middle of a crazy period where because of the war, raw material prices are going up. We h ave a dedicated team which works very professionally on identifying where are the risks

items.statement: Non-integrated steel (mini-mills, induction furnaces) and aluminium are major growth areas; dedicated sales teams created for both.
items.quote: We consider that as a major growth area for us. And to give you an example, we recently created a dedicated sales team for aluminium, because we see that as a major growth area.

items.statement: Indian steel growth next 5-10 years driven by blast furnaces (ultra-mega), not EAF; Vesuvius well positioned in both routes via caster refractories.
items.quote: if you look at what is happening in the Indian steel industry, unlike Europe, most of the growth that is going to come in the next 5 to 10 years is not in EAF, it is in blast furnace, ultra mega blast furnace s. So, we are well positioned in both the areas

items.statement: Specific refractory consumption (kg/ton steel) near plateau; value creation via technology (e.g., isostatic products at 2x price) offsets volume decline.
items.quote: We do not see today, there is still progress, if only because our own products are making progress, but the pace at which specific consumption of refractory is improving is absolutely not what it used to be over the past 30 years. So we are not very far from plateauing.

items.statement: Decarbonization (hydrogen, EAF shift) not material in India for foreseeable future; scrap generation insufficient for EAF growth; impact on refractories neutral.
items.quote: In particular, it is not happening in India. There is some talk in India, but the reality is it is not happening at all. And when you see, if you split the India steel production into three segments, induction furnace, blast furnaces, and electric furnaces, the one growing t he slowest is electric furnaces

items.statement: M&A not in DNA; growth funded via internal capex from strong balance sheet; no revision of past 1000 Cr capex guidance, likely to exceed.
items.quote: We will continue and probably we will far exceed the numbers which I mentioned some time ago in terms of capex in India for both Foseco India and Vesuvius India.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet maintained deliberately to fund growth; dividends limited to preserve investment capacity.
items.quote: We want to be ready to invest when we need. We do not need to go to the bank, we do not need to take a loan, we want to maintain a very s trong balance sheet in India because we know already that the 10 years to come will be a land of opportunity for Vesuvius India in India

items.statement: Exports not a major growth driver; "local for local" model; flow control footprint optimized globally, advanced refractories too bulky to ship economically.
items.quote: Vesuvius group really believes in local for local. That model has worked very well in the past, and we believe it will work in the future. So exports, we will grow, but it is not a major part of our growth story.

items.statement: Vesuvius Operating System drives machine utilization; capex approved only after proving no more debottlenecking possible ("last ounce of juice").

items.statement: Q4 slippages seasonal from agri and SME, 850 cr recovered, no structural concern
items.quote: Q4 slippages is not a matter of concern and from these slippages, we have pulled back almost 850 crores as we speak. That means there is no structural issue in terms of asset quality

items.statement: Gross NPA 1.49% (-33 bps YoY), Net NPA 0.39% (-8 bps YoY), PCR 74.36%
items.quote: The asset quality continues to be industry leading with gross NPAs at 1.49%, improving by 33 basis points and net NPA at 0.39%, further improving by 8 basis points on year-on-year basis. The PCR was at 74.36%

items.statement: Middle East exposure wholesale, 98%+ sovereign/bank, no asset quality concern
items.quote: the corporate book, what we have is 98% plus, is either sovereign, banks or sovereign-related exposures. We are not concerned about any corporate exposure in Middle East for these three branches

items.statement: Project Saral operations re-engineering to simplify customer journey and release capacity
items.quote: We are simplifying the bank at scale through Project Saral which I mentioned earlier with you, our operations process re -engineering initiative. The larger objective is to simplify the customer journey and release capacity within the system

items.statement: Processing fee up 50% retail, 30-35% corporate by reducing concessions, not raising rates
items.quote: today, we have almost in the retail operations, we have had a growth of 50% in processing fee and the corporate book, almost 30-35%. So, I think, we are increasing our field staff to be more proactive in terms of negotiating on that

items.statement: YONO new registrations 4 cr in 3 months, total users >10 cr, 66% new savings accounts via YONO
items.quote: The strong adoption of a new YONO, crossing 4 crore registration within three months of launch and bringing total users above 10 crores confirms that digital -first banking is now deeply embedded in customer behaviour. 66% of new savings accounts originating on YONO platform in FY26

items.statement: SBI holds 7.3% NSE, in-principle consent for OFS participation, listing to unlock reserves
items.quote: Within the group we have around 7.3% holding. But Bank itself would be keen on participating in the OFS. We have given our in -principal consent to them

items.statement: SBI AMC listing targeted this FY for CET1 capital augmentation
items.quote: we have embarked on listing SBI AMC and hopefully in this financial year we will be able to complete, which will result in capital augmentation, CET-1

items.statement: CAR 15.4% (+115 bps YoY), enough headroom for credit growth, can fund ~12 trn credit growth
items.quote: Strengthening our capital position, our C AR has improved by 115 basis points year -on-year and stands at 15.4%, which is well above the regulatory requirements. The bank has enough headroom to address future credit growth requirements

items.statement: Deposits grew 11.03% YoY (+6 trn), retail term deposits +14.77%, savings +10.6%, foreign deposits +12.7%
items.quote: We achieved resilient deposit growth of 11.03% year-on-year by about Rs 6 trillion driven by strong inflows in retail term deposits which grew by 14.77% and a double -digit savings account growth at 10.6%

items.statement: CASA ratio 39.46% (+33 bps QoQ)
items.quote: Despite competitive environment, a 39.46% CASA ratio, which is an improvement of 33 basis points quarter-on-quarter, sustains our low-cost funding advantage

items.statement: Domestic credit-deposit ratio 73.08% (+337 bps YoY)
items.quote: The domestic credit deposit ratio was 73.08% at the end of FY26, an improvement of 337 basis points year -on-year

items.statement: ROA >1%, ROE 18.5% at end Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our emphasis has always been on efficiency and return matrix, with ROA consistently greater than 1% and ROE at 18.5% at the end of Q4 FY26

items.statement: ECLGS 5.0 limit assessed at 70-80k cr for MSME/non-MSME, utilization expected 30-40%
items.quote: My assessment of 70,000 to 80,000 crores is the full limit which is available to MSMEs and other non-MSME customers. Our assessment also indicates that not more than 30%, in the worst case 30-40% people will be utilizing it

items.statement: Treasury expects 10-yr G-sec yield range 6.75-6.90% unless West Asia/fiscal shock
items.quote: our treasury holds a view that State Bank of India May 08, 2026 it would be in the range of 6.75 to 6.9, not beyond that, unless the West Asian conflict or any other fiscal imbalances create a problem

items.statement: Technology risk systemic, AI-driven cyber threats, industry moving to coordinated resilience frameworks
items.quote: Technology risk is now becoming a systemic risk. The emergence of advanced AI models capable of identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities at scale has fundamentally changed the cybersecurity paradigm

items.statement: Focus on continuous training and inclusive culture for future-ready workforce
items.quote: Most importantly, we are empowering our people with continuous training and inclusive culture to build a motivated, future-ready workforce in this dynamic environment

items.statement: Subsidiaries delivering consistent performance, will nurture for shareholder value
items.quote: Further, our subsidiaries are demonstrating consistent performance and are driving stakeholder value through digital expansion, product innovation and improved customer experience. We will continue to nurture these subsidiaries

items.statement: Guidance for minimum 15% ROE through cycles
items.quote: Through the cycles we would like to ensure 15% return on equity to our investor's minimum.

items.statement: Target 1% market share increase per district annually to reach 25% GDP share in 4-5 years
items.quote: Every district we would like to grow 1%. I am very glad whenever I travel in the field, the lowest officer in the bank also is aware of market share. So, we are trying to improve the market share in each district. I think this is a great strategic shift which is happening. 25% is a little farther, but we would like to move 1% every year, that means 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance of 13-15% for FY27
items.quote: And you have guided for a credit growth of about 13 -15% for FY27

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guidance to remain below 50%
items.quote: See, our effort is to keep cost -to-income ratio contained below 50. I think this is the guidance which we have given.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 50 basis points for FY27
items.quote: No, 50 basis point credit cost is something what we have been guiding for the last three years. We continue to do that.

items.statement: Domestic NIM guidance to remain above 3% for FY27
items.quote: NII guidance we do not give. But NIM, as I said, our guidance for domestic NIM is to remain above 3%.

items.statement: ROA guidance of 1% plus through cycles maintained despite ECL transition
items.quote: We are still saying that 1% through the cycles.

items.statement: NIM improvement to be driven by yield and advances management, asset mix changes, and spread increases
items.quote: You are right. I think it will be more in terms of the yield and advances management, we would be looking at asset mix and also increasing spreads wherever it is feasible, both on the corporate side as well as retail sides.

items.statement: Gold loans yield 8.5-8.75% with zero risk weight and near-zero NPA, LTV at 52%
items.quote: I think 8.5 to 8.75 is something what we get on this. 9% is a good yield for a product which does not require any capital allocation at all and wit h almost zero NPA

items.statement: Term deposit repricing lower mostly done with some residual tail end
items.quote: Some residual tail end, that's all, but mostly done.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth of 15% in last two quarters driven by market-to-bank shift; guidance 12-13% for corporate, 13-15% overall driven by RAM
items.quote: So, the part moment also, as I mentioned, from market to bank, if the market improves, probably the reversal will happen. So, that's the reason our corporate guidance is 12 to 13% is what we are looking at. And our 13 to 15% will be primarily driven by the RAM. RAM growth.

items.statement: Strong pipeline in transmission, battery energy storage, data centres, pump storage hydro, and smart metering
items.quote: Transmission of course, what sir has said there is a lot of potential. But I would also point out to battery energy storage systems. We have got a large number of proposals which we are processing. We also have the data centre is another activity where we have got a large number of cases we are looking at.

items.statement: CHAKRA initiative for sunrise sectors (green hydrogen, data centres, renewables, semiconductors, small modular reactors) with composite structures
items.quote: We have started an initiative called CHAKRA. This is to support all sunrise sectors, whether it is green hydrogen or whether it is data centres, whether it is new renewable energy models which are emerging. Or even small modular reactors which government has been talking about , semiconductors.

items.statement: Funding both infrastructure and GPU fit-out for data centres, focusing on hyperscaler model
items.quote: We look at the clients which are there. The way it is being presented here is more like a developer story because the developer creates the shell and ultimately the fit -out is done by the ultimate user. And we are focusing largely on the hyperscaler model because that's where the demand is assured and the client quality is assured

items.statement: Redeploying branch workforce into sales and upselling training as transactions move to alternate channels
items.quote: We are redeploying some of the workforce into sales , and train our workforce in the branches for upselling. So, this is something what is happening overall.

items.statement: Current account deposits: 21% decline in government CA, 23% growth in non-government CA; March '25 had 50,000 crore government inflow not repeated
items.quote: We have had 21% decline in the government current account deposits in the last year, whereas we completely pivoted towards non-governmental current account, where we had 23% growth rate in the current account.

items.statement: Non-fund credit exposure provisioning per RBI guidelines effective 1/04/27
items.quote: Provisioning a Non -Fund credit exposure shall be completed as per RBI guidelines, effective from 1/04/27. I think they also attract provision.

items.statement: DICGC premium savings next year but amount not disclosable per regulation
items.quote: Sorry, as per the regulation, we are not supposed to disclose that. We will get benefited definitely, but this is not a disclosable item.

items.statement: Savings bank deposits grew ~10% on large base; ABCD campaign driving deposit mobilization
items.quote: And as I mentioned, savings Bank, State Bank of India May 08, 2026 we have witnessed a good growth of almost double digit, 10% growth on a very large base of savings bank

items.statement: West Asia conflict impact on credit growth uncertain; credit growth linked to macros (6.5-6.9% GDP, 4% inflation, 10.5-11% nominal GDP)
items.quote: I think as it stands, it looks good. Except that how this West Asia conflict, how much it lingers and if we do not factor in that at this moment, I think 13 -15% seems to be a feasible option. See, at the same time, as I keep mentioning, the credit growth i s a function of

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around INR 200 crores, similar to FY26 level
items.quote: Last year, as I said, we have invested almost close to INR 200 crores, which will give some kind of increased businesses, which we have already taken some a year in advance.

items.statement: Invested close to INR 200 crores in capacity expansion across business lines in FY26
items.quote: During the year, we have invested close to INR 200 crores in capacity expansion across various business lines, reinforcing our commitment to scaling our o perations and meeting the growing market

items.statement: SPR Takahata setting up new facility at Neemrana; SPR TGPEL expanding Noida plant; Phase 3 expansion at SPL Pithampur; capacity additions at Ghaziabad and Pathredi
items.quote: Further, to take care of increasing demand from our customers, SPR Takahata is in the process of setting up a new manufacturing facility at Neemrana. And SPR TGPEL is also increasing its capacities at its Noida plant.

items.statement: Healthy pipeline with programs for hybrid platforms launching 2029-2030; new business wins in precision injection molding for anti-skid braking systems
items.quote: And we are happy to state that we are working on programs which are going to see the light of the day maybe in 2029, 2030. So, as I see it, we have a very healthy pipeline.

items.statement: Antolin EBITDA was 9-10% pre-acquisition, improving post-takeover; target to reach standalone margins (20%+) within 3 years via synergies, in-sourcing, new tech
items.quote: We already see the improvement in the first quarter, and it has started coming to very healthy levels. So, thank you very much.

items.statement: FY26 domestic demand strong across all segments (2W, 3W, tractors, CV, gensets) growing 10-11%; export flat at 1-1.5% growth due to geopolitical issues
items.quote: Overall growth has been in the region of around 10% - 11%. And if you really see the growth has come across all segments, whether it is 2 -wheelers, 3-wheelers, tractors, even standalone gensets and also all the commercial vehicles.

items.statement: Powertrain-agnostic businesses contributed ~35% of consolidated total income in Q4; ~60% of business not directly impacted by powertrain changes
items.quote: Notably, powertrain agnostic businesses contributed around 35% of our consolidated total income during the quarter, underscoring our diversified and future -ready portfolio.

items.statement: Commodity prices (aluminium up ~40%) passed through to customers with ~1 quarter lag; energy and labour not major issues
items.quote: Commodity prices have been rising up right from the last quarter. And we have seen that aluminium prices have gone as high as 40% higher than the base rate that was existing at that point in time.

items.statement: NCDs of INR 500 cr (18 months) and INR 500 cr (24 months) for Antolin acquisition; plan to repay on schedule, no prepayment
items.quote: So as far as the NCDs are concerned, we have two -time frames. One INR500 crores is for 18 months and INR500 crores is for 24 months. We plan to repay it on time.

items.statement: QIP of INR 1000 crores planned for organic and inorganic growth; not for debt repayment; promoters not participating
items.quote: The QIP is not being raised for repaying the loan. As you know we are already operating on a low debt equity ratio. But we are still hungry to grow our business, and we are still hungry to look at other options.

items.statement: Acquired 3 Antolin India entities (Jan 2026) and Karna Intertech; actively integrating for synergies; evaluating further tech-focused acquisitions
items.quote: A highlight of the year was our strategic expansion into the automotive interiors and lighting segment through the successful acquisition of three Indian entities of the Antolin Group.

items.statement: Interim dividend INR 5/share paid Feb 2026; final dividend INR 5/share recommended subject to AGM approval
items.quote: In addition to the interim dividend of INR5 per share already paid in February 2026, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR5 per share, subject to shareholders' approval in ensuing AGM.

items.statement: Wage code impact: standalone ~INR 23 cr, consolidated ~INR 27 cr; already factored in financials; no labour disruptions due to higher-than-minimum wages
items.quote: Standalone is almost to a tune of around INR 23 odd crores and consolidated is around INR 27 odd crores. And all of this has been consi dered in both our consolidated results as well as the stand-alone results.

items.statement: EV penetration estimated 15-17% by 2030 on 6% CAGR; ICE+hybrid to remain dominant; multiple powertrains to coexist
items.quote: I still think that the EV business will be anywhere between 15% to 17% penetration by 2030, but this will be at a backdrop on a CAGR growth of around 6%.

items.statement: Exports flat (1-1.5% growth) due to Ukraine war, Middle East tensions, Europe degrowth; retained market share; new product lines and customers being developed
items.quote: Yes. So, it's no big surprise that exports are really in a tough situation with the Ukraine war continuing, with the kind of situation that exists in the European region, there's hardly any growth.

items.statement: Precision injection molding remains niche; outgrowing market (11% vs 6-7% industry); new tech wins (anti-skid braking components) driving growth
items.quote: So, if you really see the overall market has grown by around anywhere between 6% to 7% if I do a combined weighted av erage kind of a growth for all segments of the business, whether it is 2-wheeler, 4-wheeler, tractors, commercial vehicles and everything.

items.statement: GST 2.0 and income tax reforms supported demand recovery in H2 FY26; Delhi ICE ban from 2028 noted; ethanol blending may rise to 85%
items.quote: This momentum was supported by favourable macroeconomic factors domestically, including the introduction of GST 2.0, income tax reforms and reduced financing costs.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Middle East, Ukraine) affecting exports and commodity prices; commodity pass-through has ~1 quarter lag; customer approvals needed for margin improvement
items.quote: And we have seen that aluminium prices have gone as high as 40% higher than the base rate that was existing at that point in time. And most of the other areas also, commodities have increased.

items.statement: ESG recognition: CDP B rating 2025, EcoVadis bronze (top 25%), Dun & Bradstreet ESG rating 2 (highest in India), TÜV certified, ACMA Gold, CII significant achievement
items.quote: During the year, our climate and water disclosures were awarded a CDP B rating for 2025, and our greenhouse gas emissions were independently assured in line with ISO 17029, underscoring the credibility of our sustainability data.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of ~40% CAGR for next 3 years; EBITDA margins expected to remain stable in FY27
items.quote: Historically, we've been maintaining one stand that we would be growing at about 40% CAGR for next 3 years. First year has already passed by with an intention of margins being stable because of the reason that we have yet not manufactured a 400KV class transformer and a 765KV class transformer under the brand name of Atlanta Electricals.

items.statement: Vadod facility utilization target 65% in FY27, 100% in FY28
items.quote: We expect it to be 65% in this particular year and then eventually taking it to 100% in the next financial year.

items.statement: Export revenue target 15% of total revenue within 3 years
items.quote: We have been maintaining this trend that in next 3 years' time, we have this target of taking our exports to 15% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Net working capital days expected to increase to 80-90 days in FY27 and FY28 from ~64 days in FY26
items.quote: Going forward in FY27 and FY28, our net working capital days will go up around 80s and 90s. However, during FY26, we could maintain our net working capital days at around 64.

items.statement: FY26 new orders INR2,507 crores; unexecuted order book INR2,493 crores as of 31 March 2026 with higher 220kV/EHV share
items.quote: Team Atlanta booked INR2,507 crores of new order during FY26, which elevated our unexecuted order book on 31st March 2026 to INR2,493 crores, providing strong execution visibility going into FY27.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 18.6% (+300bps YoY); Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 19.99%; management expects margins stable in FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for full year FY '26 stood at INR344.4 crores, up 77.9% year-on-year with EBITDA margin expanding to 18.6% compared to 15.6% in FY '25, reflecting an expansion of 300 basis points.

items.statement: 400kV/765kV products expected to carry ~200bps higher margin vs 220kV, but overall FY27 margins guided stable due to prototype costs
items.quote: We expect that 400 and 765KV class would be around 200 basis points higher. But as of today in the current last financial year numbers, there are no 400KV class products and there are no revenue coming in for 400KV class products.

items.statement: FY27 capex: IDT facility INR65 crores at Vadod (5,000 MVA); tank & radiator backward integration INR170-180 crores near Vadod; funded by internal accruals, term loan if needed
items.quote: So, for IDT it is around INR65 crores of capex and for backward integration, it is INR170 to INR180 crores of the capex.

items.statement: Vadod unit (30,000 MVA nameplate) ran at ~39% utilization in 7 months of FY26; produced 6,960 MVA; Ankhi unit produced 580 MVA in 3 months
items.quote: On an annual basis, for the seven months of operation, unit four operated at approximately 39% of the nameplate capacity, which is 30,000 MVA.

items.statement: Unit 6 (IDT facility) to commence operations in FY27, targeting before end of calendar year 2026, adding 5,000 MVA capacity
items.quote: We will commence operations at Unit 6, our dedicated IDT transformer facility during FY27. We are working towards making this facility operational before end of this calendar year.

items.statement: 220kV class now ~52% of FY26 revenue; first 400kV order secured; 765kV prototype planned at Ankhi
items.quote: This margin expansion is structural in nature, driven by operating leverage from higher volumes, a richer product mix tilting towards 220KV class, which now constitutes nearly 52% of our revenue.

items.statement: Green transformers (ester oil) enabled continued production during mineral oil shortage in Q4 FY26; PGCIL approval for 400kV at Vadod received 2 April 2026
items.quote: We received PGCIL approval, which was according to us was the fastest in the industry. The single biggest operation milestone in the FY26 is the PGCIL approval for the manufacturing of transformers up to 400KV at our unit four, which is Vadod facility. We received this approval on 2nd April 2026.

items.statement: Domestic demand scaling in BESS, data centers, renewables; transformer requirement 8-11x GW generation; BESS adds incremental demand
items.quote: The thumb rule says it is anywhere between 8 to 11 times the gigawatt capacity gets added, the transformer capacity gets added in various KV classes. This thumb rule generally would tend to increase because battery energy storage systems were never a thumb rul

items.quote: Approximately 75% of the order is on with the price variation clause and rest of the orders are without price variation clause.

items.statement: Commodity price increases (copper, aluminium, crude, fabricated components) passed through via price variation clauses; no margin hit in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are able to, since majority of our contracts are on with the price variation formula, we are able to pass on the majority cost to our customers.

items.statement: Conductor supply improving with new domestic capacity; RIP bushing supply easing; OIP bushing supply tight - managing via advance orders and new vendors
items.quote: We have been telling on the last couple of calls that the situation around the supply of conductors is improving because many of the manufacturers, Indian manufacturers who had announced their plans to expand capacities, those expanded facilities came to life and we have started now taking the supplies.

items.statement: All term debt (INR340 crores) fully repaid by 31 March 2026 using IPO proceeds and internal accruals; debt-free; CRISIL A stable / A1 reaffirmed
items.quote: As of 31st March '26, the closing balance on all term loans is nil. This has been completely repaid through a combination of IPO proceeds, internal accruals, and general corporate purpose fund, ahead of the original repayment schedule.

items.statement: FY26 operating cash flow INR184 crores; year-end inventory deliberately drawn down for planned maintenance shutdowns in early April
items.quote: Our operating cash flow for FY '26 is healthy at INR184 crores, reflective of the strong underlying business momentum and disciplined working capital management.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR400 crores: INR395.46 crores deployed by 31 March 2026 (INR79.12 cr Vadod loan, INR210 cr WC, INR85 cr BTW loan, INR21.31 cr expenses); INR4.54 cr balance
items.quote: Out of the INR400 crores fresh issue, approximately INR395.46 crores has been deployed as of 31st March 2026. items.statement: Merger of Atlanta Trafo Limited with Atlanta Electricals Limited to commence shortly
items.quote: Within a short span, we shall also be commencing the procedure of merging Atlanta Trafo Limited with Atlanta Electricals Limited.

items.statement: FY26 production 22,943 MVA across 5 units; Vadod 6,960 MVA (7 months), Ankhi 580 MVA (3 months); legacy units at high utilization
items.quote: Across all five manufacturing units, the team of Atlanta Electricals produced a total of 22,943 MVAs in financial year '26.

items.statement: Vadod facility payback on track for 3-4 years vs industry 5-7 years; contributed INR495 crores revenue in first 7 months
items.quote: Vadod alone contributed nearly INR495 crores of revenue in first seven months of operation. Based on this trajectory, we are well on the course to achieve payback in three to four years' timeline.

items.statement: Mineral oil shortage in Q4 FY26 due to West Asian conflict; managed via green transformer flexibility and inventory planning
items.quote: Despite the temporary shortage of mineral oil during quarter four of FY26 arising from the ongoing West Asian conflict, we were able to maintain strong production and dispatch momentum due to our proactive forward planning.

items.statement: First sizeable export order received in FY26; targeting systematic market entry with physical presence in select markets; export lead times longer than domestic
items.quote: The first sizeable export order was received in FY26, which has given us a strong foundation to build upon. We shall now be pursuing other markets in a systematic way. We shall choose markets with an intent of staying long in those territories.

items.statement: Industry capacity additions driven by demand (500GW by 2030, 900GW by 2035 targets); demand to exceed supply for at least 5 years
items.quote: India has been setting up newer and newer targets and a higher and higher targets for the power generation. So, we have been hearing 500 gigawatts by 2030. items.quote: As on March 31st, 2026, our order book stood at over 125 crores, providing strong revenue visibility and a solid foundation for future growth.

items.statement: Order book doubled year-on-year from approximately 62 crores to over 125 crores
items.quote: Yes, it has doubled, and that is the only way we could have performed, you know, and...

items.statement: All 125 crores of current order book expected to convert to revenue in FY27 given 10-12 month project gestation period
items.quote: So all 125 crores will get consumed within this year itself.

items.quote: But this is what the narration has been very beginning that we are looking for at least 30 to 40% growth overall.

items.quote: One was the logistic cost and Agastya Dave: Anuj Dosajh: the second was the raw material cost itself, typically the metal cost which went as high as 25 to 40 % and especially the specialised metal, you know, which are being used

items.quote: We will be quite, again, like I said, it will be quite circumspect in our approach towards taking orders which are meaningful in terms of bottom line too. items.statement: Strong demand outlook driven by manufacturing expansion, water scarcity, and stricter environmental compliance across multiple industrial sectors
items.quote: There are quite a few sectors, you know, India is now, I feel, putting in more manufacturing units and they are focusing on that. And the water becoming scarcer is, and the compliance is getting stronger. I think, yes, we are in for a good period of time, at least I think so.

items.statement: Marquee order wins from Reliance Consumer Products, L&T, CRD Food Products, Bhartiyam Beverages, and Pragati Power Corporation in FY26

items.statement: Not reliant on single client; working with multiple large companies directly and indirectly, with repeat orders from existing blue-chip customers

items.statement: Cash and bank balance increased to 35.06 crores as of March 31, 2026; working capital at 61.72 crores supporting growing operations
items.quote: Our cash and bank balance increased to 35.06 crores as of March 31st, 2026, while working capital stood at 61.72 crores, supporting the company's growing scale of operations and execution pipeline.

items.statement: Significant portion of cash deployed as fixed deposits for non-fund based guarantees (ABGs, retention BGs, PBGs) required by large clients
items.quote: Most of this fund is directed towards the, you know, making fixed deposits for the for for the act as collaterals towards submission of a non-fund based guarantees.

items.statement: No major capex or acquisition plans; cash primarily used for bank guarantee margins; seeking higher non-fund based limits from bankers
items.quote: We are speaking to our bankers for a higher limit. But then, like I said, if we are doing most of these jobs, they demand this kind of, you need margins and collaterals for, so you need that kind of fund to be invested into the bank also.

items.statement: Focus remains primarily on domestic India market; explored Gulf states but found them unsuitable; India seen as more stable
items.quote: Well, I think India is the most stable. India is more stable than supposed stability in other countries. There was a lot of, you know, we had also thought of and made endorses in the Gulf states, but then that has turned out to be totally anti-modal to our thought process.

items.statement: Specialized in custom-built zero liquid discharge, wastewater recycling and reuse for industrial sector; not in municipal/desalination or household segments
items.quote: We are typically into custom built jobs which are for zero liquid discharge. Let me mention something to you. items.quote: It is a privilege for me to address all of you as I take over as the CEO of Alicon Castalloy effective 1st of April 2026.

items.statement: Significant talent addition across sales, technology, program management, manufacturing, supply chain, tool manufacturing, operational excellence, HR
items.quote: Over recent months, we have significantly strengthened our leadership team across functions, including sales and marketing, product and process technology, program management, manufacturing, supply chain, tool manufacturing, operational excellence and human resource.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure expected in FY27 from aluminum price volatility, energy costs, freight, packaging, currency, and labour cost increases
items.quote: Consequently, these factors could exert some pressure on the margins, as we move into FY 2027.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: 2-wheeler ~42%, PV ~34%, CV ~17-18%, non-auto ~5-6%; deemed exports ~20%
items.quote: If I s ee segment-wise bifurcation for this year, two -wheeler, yes, there was a little up because the market pull up. So, it was near about 42%, followed by passenger at 34%, roughly 17% to 18% was commercial. And also, we noticed a little traction in the non -auto to 5% to 6

items.statement: JLR Range Rover program: 18-month development delay resolved; vehicle manufacturing started; launch imminent; supplies commenced
items.quote: The good news is we have recently seen the vehicle. We had an opportunity while we were in JLR. The vehicle is due to come on the roads very soon. Our supplies have started.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 1500 crores for Vision 2028
items.quote: As we have stated in our Vision and what we have committed in the last three years that they will achieve INR 1500 crores, we are working on it and we will achieve it.

items.statement: Organic growth target 15-18% CAGR, inorganic to push to 20% CAGR over three years
items.quote: We continue to achieve the Vision 2028. However, we aim to further accelerate the growth target from 15% CAGR to 20% CAGR in the next three years and it is expected to be meaningfully supported by a well-defined acquisition framework.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided range 17-18%, actual FY26 19.6%
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded upward of 19% for both Quarter and FY26 driven by efficient operational performance surpassing our guided range of 17% to 18%.

items.statement: Annual capex requirement INR 30-35 crores including frontend and backend
items.quote: So, not much. As we said close to around INR 30 crores to INR 35 crores is the requirement for CAPEX that includes the frontend as well as the backend on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: KKCL manufacturing operating at 100% efficiency, no immediate plan to absorb Kraus manufacturing
items.quote: Currently, KKCL is only operating at 100% efficiency structure.

items.statement: Net 57 EBOs added in FY26, total 666 stores as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: In line with our strategy to expand our brand footprint, we added net 57 EBOs in FY26, taking our total to 666 stores as on March 31, 2026.

items.statement: Store addition target 50-70 net EBOs for full year
items.quote: Full year should be around net around 50 to 70 odd stores.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to stay in 41-43% range going forward
items.quote: But going forward also, the gross margin should stay anywhere between 41 to 43 range.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 19.6% for FY26, up from guided 17-18%
items.quote: Our execution-led operational discipline enabled us to grow at scale while protecting profitability resulting in a strong EBITDA margin of 19.6% for FY26.

items.statement: Apparel volume growth 16% YoY consolidated in FY26
items.quote: Apparel volume growth on a consolidated basis saw an encouraging growth of 16% year-on-year driven by strong design capabilities and sustained consumer demand for our products.

items.statement: Retail grew 24% YoY, non-retail 17% YoY in FY26
items.quote: For FY26, retail grew 24% and non-retail grew 17% year-on-year underscoring consistent broad-based momentum across formats.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth 6.8% in Q4 FY26 and 9.4% for FY26
items.quote: The SSG for Q4 FY26 is 6.8% and for the year FY26 is 9.4%.

items.statement: Working capital days target 130-140 days overall, Kraus slightly higher
items.quote: Okay. The working capital should stay anywhere between a limit of 130 to 140 odd days.

items.statement: No price hikes taken yet, room for future increases if needed
items.quote: We have not taken any price hike yet. We operate at the same prices. The product mix changes a little bit. That is up to season-to-season, of course. But we have not done any price hike. So, we have a room in future if we have to hike the prices, we have that room.

items.statement: May absorb 1-2% margin hit from raw material inflation to protect revenue and market share
items.quote: Even if we have to take a hit of 1% or 2%, the company is ready to take that kind of hit.

items.statement: GST impact neutral for FY26 after passing benefit to consumers in Q3
items.quote: Going forward or maybe for FY26, we feel that the impact of GST is neutral for the company.

items.statement: Exports not significant, mainly Middle East and Saudi, expected to remain constant or degrow next year
items.quote: And we think that the exports are going to remain constant or may degrew for the next year.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions across segments, genders, price points; evaluating on ROCE and synergy
items.quote: We are also open for our competing categories also, as well as premium, as well as the value segment. We are even open for any gender specific.

items.statement: No change in Kraus 50% stake for first five years, further acquisition possible after
items.quote: There is nothing changed for the first five years period. After that, there can be some.

items.statement: No buyback planned due to 74% promoter holding, dividend policy continues
items.quote: It's a company policy. Yes, already the promoter has 74 point somepercentage. So, right now we are not thinking about the buyback.

items.statement: Denim mix intended at 45-48%, down from historical 60%, expected to stay similar
items.quote: We have intended and tried to derisk the entire category mix and come down to close to around 45 or 48. I think with the retail expansion, all the categories move in the similar percentage structure. So, I think it should stay in the similar mix of what it is as of today.

items.statement: Full price sales around 60%
items.quote: Full price sales was close to around 60%.

items.statement: E-commerce growing in line with company growth
items.quote: It is in line with the company.

items.statement: Kraus manufacturing fully outsourced, no immediate plan to bring in-house
items.quote: currently, everything is outsourced in terms of manufacturing, correct, right? Hemant Jain: Yes

items.statement: Other income annualized expected INR 30-35 crores, Q4 decline due to mark-to-market
items.quote: So, if you look at the annualized number our other income should stay somewhere between INR 30 crores to INR 35 crores.

items.statement: War situation creates uncertainty on oil and cotton prices, day-to-day monitoring
items.quote: What would happen, what would the situation be? How the prices of oil will behave or how the cotton prices will behave. As of now our endeavor was to not lose the revenue and we should not reduce our market share.

items.statement: Targets INR 600 crore disbursements and INR 1,300-1,400 crore AUM for FY27, optimistic on INR 1,500 crore
items.quote: With the discussion on the disbursement number, we are targeting of approximately INR 600 crores of disbursement for this year. So, this is our target.

items.statement: Targets INR 2,000-2,500 crore AUM in next 2.5-3 years; long-term vision INR 10,000-20,000 crore
items.quote: We think that if our branch makes around INR 25 crores, then our target for the branch is around INR 110 crores. So, we should have a book of INR 2000 crores, INR 2500 crores within the next two and a half years, three years.

items.statement: Plans 10-15 new branches in Tamil Nadu and Telangana by end of FY27; no expansion in existing states
items.quote: We are also planning our expansion in the states of Tamil Nadu and Telangana. With that, it will take time for us to do our research. And by the end of this year, we will be present in the states of Tamil Nadu and Telangana. But we are planning for approximately 10 to 15 new branches in these particular states.

items.statement: Expects NIMs to sustain around 11%
items.quote: Somewhere around 11% only.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing expected to decline from 10.88% to around 10.70% over next 1-2 years
items.quote: The correct cost of borrowing for Q4 FY26 is 10.88%. Going forward, over the next one to two years, the expectation is that it may decline from 10.88% to around 10.70%.

items.statement: AUM grew 37% YoY to INR 1,042 crore in FY26; disbursements grew 45% YoY to INR 443.54 crore
items.quote: As of Financial Year 2026, our assets under management stand at INR 1042 crores, reflecting a strong growth of 37% year-on-year. Disbursements for the year grew by 45% year-on-year to INR 443.54 crores reflecting healthy demand momentum across our operating geographies.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 1.77% from 1.84%; NNPA at 0.65%; Stage-1 assets 93.05%, Stage-2 5.18%, Stage-3 1.77%
items.quote: Asset quality continued to remain stable and healthy. GNPA improved to 1.77% compared to 1.84% last year. While NNPA stood at 0.65% reflecting prudent underwriting standards and strong correction efficiency.

items.statement: Average LTV maintained at 50.7% in Q4 FY26, up from 46.6% YoY due to product nature, not strategy
items.quote: Basically, it is not a strategy and there is no risk profile to it. It is more about the nature of the product that we are into. And to be in the market and to understand that it is the nature of the housing finance product is actually driving us from a 46 LTV, 47 LTV to 50 something LTV.

items.statement: 97% of EMI collections via banking channels; cheque bounce rate 14-15%, 90% recovered within 30 days; cash collections only 4-5%
items.quote: Around 97% of our collections come through banking channels, and the majority of our repayments are received through this route. We also have a dedicated collections and efficiency team in place. Initially, our cheque bounce rate is around 14%–15%. After that, we have a full-fledged call center team that follows up with customers. As a result, only around 2%–3% remains pending, while the rest of t

items.statement: Rating upgraded to A- Stable by Acuité; leverage currently below 5-6x bank limit, may raise equity in Q4 FY27 or Q1-Q2 FY28 if leverage crosses 5-6x
items.quote: Acuité rating has upgraded our long-term credit rating and made it A- Stable which reflects our improving business fundamentals, stable asset quality and strong capitalization.

items.statement: May consider raising equity in Q4 FY27 or Q1-Q2 FY28 once leverage crosses 5-6x range
items.quote: Therefore, once our leverage crosses the 5x–6x range, we will certainly look at raising additional equity. In my view, if this year progresses well and things remain on track, we may consider raising equity in the fourth quarter. Otherwise, we would look to raise equity in the first or second quarter of the following year.

items.statement: Healthy demand momentum across operating geographies; 41% YoY increase in average ticket size to INR 15.44 lakh driven by higher construction costs and expansion into newer markets
items.quote: We also witnessed a 41% year-on-year increase in average ticket size to INR 15.44 lakh during the quarter primarily driven by expansion into newer markets and higher construction costs.

items.statement: Ticket size increase driven by higher property prices and construction costs, not customer profile shift; self-employed remain 79% of customers
items.quote: Sir, I think it is more of the purchase has increased, the construction cost has increased, and the customer profile remains the same for us. And I do not see any difference in that we are getting very new or different profiles in comparison to the urban profiles, but the profile remains the same.

items.statement: Focus on underserved self-employed in rural/semi-urban; 79% self-employed, 94% rural/semi-urban; proprietary underwriting templates for segments like kirana, dairy, contractors
items.quote: So, we have created a lot of different profile templates. We have our own understanding, own database to understand the repayment tracks of different sectors where we are focusing on. Why we are different? So, we do not believe on assessment. Of course, when you have less documentation, right? Because you are definitely targeting to those particular segments. So, we have an understanding of assess

items.statement: AUM per branch increased to INR 10.86 crore from INR 8.44 crore; AUM per employee improved to INR 1.05 crore from INR 0.88 crore YoY
items.value: 10.86 crore per branch; 1.05 crore per employee
items.quote: AUM per branch increased to INR 10.86 crores in Quarter 4 Financial Year '26 from INR 8.44 crores in Quarter 4 Financial Year '25 while AUM per employee improved to INR 1.05 crores from INR 0.88 crores over the same period reflecting improving operational efficiency and strong skilled productivity gain.

items.statement: Expanding top management team and recruiting for expansion; IT team increased for digital transformation
items.quote: We are focusing on a better top management team as well. We are doing a lot of recruitments as well and expansion also.

items.statement: NHB guidelines allow up to 12x leverage but banks typically limit to 5-6x; will raise equity when leverage crosses 5-6x
items.quote: Further, as our AUM increases, we believe that under NHB guidelines, we can leverage up to 12x. However, in practice, banks generally do not allow leverage beyond 5x–6x. Therefore, once our leverage crosses the 5x–6x range, we will certainly look at raising additional equity.

items.statement: No material impact from macro uncertainty or monsoon on self-employed borrower segment (kirana, dairy, contractors) due to small-scale operations and conservative LTV/FOIR
items.quote: Sir, all these macro things which are happening around the world and which might be impacting India in a manner that large business houses might get affected. Those who are directly associated with the government policies, that might affect. But we are into the segment which is very small, right? We are into the segment which has and which are majorly self-employed. And with the very basic self-em

items.statement: ROE expected to remain around 12-13% over next 1-2 years
items.quote: Right. So, it is going to be same parallelly. But we are definitely optimistic on that. So, we will go around 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 63.14% from 67.49% YoY in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Operational efficiency also improved steadily with a cost to income ratio declining to 63.14% from 67.49% over the same period supported by improving sale efficiency and operating leverage.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 38.62% providing sufficient headroom for growth
items.quote: Our capital position also remained comfortable with capital adequacy at 38.62% providing sufficient headroom to support future growth.

items.statement: No significant competition impact despite rising ticket sizes; customer profile and income source unchanged
items.quote: Not really, sir, because the customer profile remains the same. The source of income remains the same. Although there is a change in the cost of construction also and the aspiration of how a house should look like. That is also changing in the sector of rural and semi-urban. So, with that sentiment, the reason of why we have an increase in the ticket size.

items.statement: Mutual funds now investing in NCDs alongside equity; reflects broad investor trust
items.quote: One of the most important achievements for us is that mutual fund companies have also invested in our NCDs. It is not very common to see investors supporting a company through both equity participation and NCD investments.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain EBITDA margin in 25%-27% range and working capital days at FY26 levels for next 1-2 years.
items.quote: We maintained a margin guidance of 25%-27% and the cash conversion cycle which we clocked in FY 26, broadly should be in line for next one, two years basically.

items.statement: Company targets 25%-30% top-line growth for FY27 driven by volume and price realization.
items.quote: That is the company aim also. We see our capacity also to be fully utilized. The company is totally driven by and working very hard to achieve the growth which you have mentioned currently.

items.statement: Strategic capex of ~INR 460 crores over next 2-3 years for new solvent fractionation facility, CBA plant, refinery expansion, and Burkina Faso raw material processing units.
items.quote: Through strategic capital expenditure commitment of approximately INR 460 crores over the next two to three years, this investment program spans setting up of a new solvent fractionation manufacturing facility for Sal, Shea, Palm, Mango and other exotic seeds and ESOS.

items.statement: Burkina Faso backward integration project capex ~INR 120 crores to eliminate seed import logistics costs (45%-60% of raw material) and improve yield.
items.quote: The Burkina Faso project, which is a backward integration, part of the project for the company's next capex plan. So, we arc envisaging these cxpenses or capex amount of around INR 120 odd crores towards our Burkina Faso project.

items.statement: Forward integration project (CBA plant, 75,000 ton solvent fractionation plant 3, 90,000 ton refinery) targets >6x asset turnover on ~INR 330-340 crores capex.
items.quote: we have given our earlier communication towards we are expecting more than 6x of asset turn on our forward integration project, which is around INR 330-340 Crores of the tofal capex amount.

items.statement: Solvent fractionation plant 2 debottlenecked 30% from 25,000 to 32,500 tons/annum; plant 1 (15,000 tons) debottlenecking planned this fiscal.
items.quote: Our solvent fractionation plant 2 increased installed capacity by 30% from 25,000 tons per annum to 32,500 tons per annum as part of an overall debottlenceking initiative.
