items.statement: Total fractionation capacity to reach 52,000 tons after both plant debottlenecking; targeting 85%-90% utilization in FY27.
items.quote: We are targeting and aiming to utilize around 85%- 90%, 85% of plant on our 52,000 tons full capacity. That is the kind of utilization we are targeting for this fiscal year.

items.statement: All capex projects targeted for commissioning by FY28 in phased manner over 2-3 year window.
items.quote: All our projects are targeted to be commissioned by the financial year 128, in that particular way. That is how we arc targeting it to spend. It is like two-three year window, we are targeting to complete it.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 27.1% (standalone), 26% (consolidated); 230 bps expansion driven by value-added mix improvement (CBE 10% to 30%) and higher plant utilization.
items.quote: EBITDA INR 367.7 crores with an EBITDA margin of 27.1%, reflecting focused product mix optimization and disciplined cost management.

items.statement: Gross margin normal range 45%-50%; consolidated gross margin temporarily lower due to subsidiary startup costs and freight.
items.quote: Anything between the 45%-50% level of gross margin is normal in the parlance of the business model. This we have repeated and cmphasized on the past as well.

items.statement: FY26 stearin volume ~8,000 tons, CBE volume ~7,500 tons; CBE contributes ~30% of revenue, value-added products (CBE + stearin) ~70%-75%.
items.quote: Stearin volume was around 8,000 reported on a full year metric ton, and CBE volume has been reported around 7,500 metric ton for full year.

items.statement: CBE share of revenue increased from 10% two years ago to 30% in FY26; value-added products (CBE + stearin) now 70%-75% of sales.
items.quote: CBE has contributed around 30% to our top linc. Along with our value-added product stearin , it is around 70%-75% to it. If you see 30% today what we have done with CBE, it was 10% fwo years ago.

items.statement: FY27 outlook strongly positive with structural growth levers: volume-led growth from debottlenecking, 5%-10% price realization benefit, and global diversification.
items.quote: Overall, the financial year 2027 is expected to be a very g00d growth year for revemues for the company, with growth primarily volume-led driven and some price realization benefit also structurally driven by the capacity expansion.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to ~125 days in FY26 from 151 days in FY25; operating cash flow INR 259 crores; inventory INR 710 crores (RM INR 420 cr, FG INR 260 cr, WIP/co-products INR 30 cr).
items.quote: Working capital cyele improved to approximately 125 days in FY 26 compared to 151 days in FY 125. Net cash flow from operating activities stood at INR 259 crores.

items.statement: ~60% of net forex exposure hedged via forwards; cumulative MTM loss INR 23.3 cr in FY26; Middle East revenue exposure only 2%-3%.
items.quote: Around a 60% of our company's net forcign exchange is currently hedged through forward contracts. It also provide carning visibility and protecting against any adverse currency movements.

items.statement: Burkina Faso project backed by government MoU; management states political risk will not affect operations.
items.quote: Sce, for that, its a govemment-backed project also because we have signed an MoU, Memorandum of Understanding, with the government of Burkina Faso. Anything politically will be not affecting the project what we are going to put up there.

items.statement: Burkina Faso processing to shift procurement from seeds to butter (45%-60% of raw material cost), saving logistics/freight and improving yield.
items.quote: Going forward, it will be on the butter perspective, which is approximately 45%-60% of the raw material. Accordingly, we are going to save the logistic cost, freight cost on our seed import from West African countries.

items.statement: Manorama Africa (promoter entity) supplied 20%-25% of raw material in FY26; similar procurement line expected to continue in FY27.
items.quote: Around 20%-25%, we bought the raw material from Manorama Africa Limited this financial year 25-26. For 127, what would it be? Tt will be ~ depends on the - which will be same line of procurement will be continued

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (West Asia, Russia-Ukraine) may cause indirect impact via higher energy/freight costs and currency volatility, but raw materials not sourced from affected regions and revenue exposure minimal.
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical tension including Iran, U.S., Russia, Ukraine or some, you know, the tariff, are expected to have anear-term indirect impact, not only on our industry, but a broader industry environment as a whole.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth 80%-90%, price growth 5%-10%; ROCE 33.6%, ROE 40.3%; annual cash profit (PAT + depreciation) INR 258.77 cr exceeds gross block INR 250 cr.
items.quote: Volume growth of this financial year '25, '26, around 80%-90% and 5%-10% is the price growth.

items.statement: QIP enabling resolution approved for up to INR 500 crores; evaluating options, will disclose when terms finalized; not yet combined with capex funding plan.
items.quote: In terms of QIP, this is an approved cnabling resolution. In relation, it could be a potential fundraise, maybe through a permissible modes and instruments and we arc currently evaluating various options.

items.statement: Nine new international subsidiaries established in FY26 (first year of operations); initial setup costs (employee, establishment, overheads) temporarily impacting consolidated margins.
items.quote: The Company has expanded to global footprint with established nine subsidiarics across different countrics and marking important strategic step towards building a diversified international presence.

items.statement: Dekel Brazil arrangement is toll processing model (pay per ton processed), no profit sharing; operations just started, minimal volume in FY26.
items.quote: No, it's a cost model thing there. It's a processing cost which the company needs to pay them for processing of the per ton of our goods. There is no agreament in terms of profit sharing which is there with the Dekel agreement.

items.statement: Revised financial statements filed due to inadvertent upload of wrong file; revision purely corrective, no financial impact.
items.quote: This revised financial statement file has been uploaded inadvertently. I's been submitted to ausure accuracy and completeness of the reported information. The revision is purely corrective in nature.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA growth of close to 30% over FY26 in FY27
items.quote: I think this year, we will be very comfortable with our growth close to 30% over this year. Over the last year, we were very comfortable, yes.

items.statement: Board approved fresh capex of INR2,700 crores for long specialty wire mill and stainless steel expansion
items.quote: The Board has approved a fresh capex is INR2,700 crores for our next phase of growth. This investment comprising 2 major projects.

items.statement: Total capex plan of around INR10,000 crores with INR2,900 crores in FY27 and INR3,000 crores in FY28
items.quote: As far as the total capex is required to be incurred is around INR10,000 crores. And this financial year, we will be incurring around INR2,900 crores from this financial year and INR3,000 crores in the next financial year and balance will be the next 2 financial years.

items.statement: Long specialty wire mill of 8 lakh tonnes at Kharagpur targeting commissioning by March 2029
items.quote: We will be setting up a long specialty wire mill with a furnace at Kharagpur with a capacity of 8 lakh tonnes at an estimated capital outlay of INR900 crores. This project is targeting to commission by 31st March 2029.

items.statement: Stainless steel expansion to 6 million tonnes at Sambalpur with downstream facilities targeting March 2029
items.quote: We're expanding our stainless steel capacity to 6 million tonnes at Sambalpur complemented by world-class downstream capability, including cold rolling mill, precision cold rolling mill, hot rolling handling and pickling line and a bright annealing line.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4% from 13.8% YoY and 12.2% QoQ
items.quote: When we talk about the EBITDA margin, 14.4%, expanded from 13.8% from the quarter 4 of the last financial year and 12.2% in quarter 3 of the last financial year.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin at 13.7% vs 13.8% in FY25 amid input cost pressure
items.quote: Full year EBITDA margin is 13.7% against 13.8% in the financial year '25, resulting amidst slight input cost pressure.

items.statement: Stainless steel EBITDA per tonne expected at INR12,000-15,000, potentially over INR18,000 with full integration
items.quote: EBITDA, generally, this is a very interesting business. So I would say, generally, it turn from around INR15,000 to INR20,000 a tonne. So but our overall calculation is in the range of INR12,000 to INR15,000.

items.statement: CRM EBITDA expected at INR10,000-11,000 per tonne and aluminum EBITDA at INR35,000-40,000 per tonne in FY27
items.quote: I think the CRM EBITDA is going to be close to INR10,000 to INR11,000 per tonne this year from the -- and the aluminum EBITDA, I think, should remain between INR35,000 to INR40,000.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand robust supported by infrastructure, manufacturing, urbanization
items.quote: The global steel demand environment remained robust and encouraging. Demand continues to support by broad-based strength across major steel consuming sector, including infrastructure-led construction activity, manufacturing activity, urbanization with spending on huge infra projects such as road, railways, power.

items.statement: Aluminum export demand oversold, unable to supply international market
items.quote: We are oversold. We are not able to supply to the international market, touchwood.

items.statement: Aluminum realization improved 16% YoY to INR4,07,461/tonne; stainless steel up ~17%; CR coil/CR sheet up ~15% to INR78,513/tonne
items.quote: Aluminum realization improved by 16% year-on-year basis, that is INR4,07,461 per tonne. Stainless steel realizations improved nearly 17% year-on basis. CR coil, CR sheet realizations rose approximately 15% on a year-on basis, that is INR78,513 per tonne.

items.statement: Aluminum margins largely pass-through; backward integration into foil stock to improve margins
items.quote: I think we should see as a pass-through, maybe because of a little bit more advantage we get because the working capital involvement and the kind of integration, what we are doing from the backward to the forward, we'll see a lot of value coming up.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced from 22 to 9 days in FY26
items.quote: reflecting a disciplined capital allocation, operational efficiency, prudent leverage management that resulted into reflection of our working capital days from 22 days to 9 days.

items.statement: Debt policy: debt not to exceed 0.5x total equity; company nearly debt-free with strong cash generation
items.quote: Our debt will not cross at any point 0.5x to the total equity in any point of circumstances. So we will follow this debt policy.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR2.7 per equity share (27% of face value) for FY26
items.quote: As you're all aware that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR2.7 per equity share, representing a 27% of the face value of INR10 each for the financial year '25-'26.

items.statement: CPCB non-compliance identified, resolved in 4-5 days; full compliance expected within 3 months
items.quote: No, no, there was some kind of error, which was identified by the Board inspection, which was resumed in 4, 5 days, and we have taken all the action. And in the time to come, we will take it more seriously and see how best we can deliver. Yes.

items.statement: ED case on coal not a concern; notice applies to major steel industry; no evidence against company
items.quote: There is absolutely not to worry because there's nothing -- they have given some letter. We are replying. And it's nothing to be worried of because there's nothing which is of an evidence or something on the statement, they have given a notice.

items.statement: Stainless steel targeting pipes/tubes, decorative, utensil, export defense markets; B2B model serving tube manufacturers
items.quote: Stainless steel basically -- yes, we are targeting the pipes and tube market, decorative market of pipes and tubes. There is a specialty pipe market also, which is for the precision pipe and all.

items.statement: FY26 sales volume 4.94 million tonnes, up 26% YoY; Q4 FY26 volume up 22% YoY
items.quote: For FY26, our sales volume stood at 4.94 million tonnes, reflecting a strong year-on-year growth of 26%. In Q4 '26, sales volume registered a growth of 22% over the smart period of last year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target 15% and new order wins INR20,000-22,000 crore
items.value: 15% revenue growth; INR20,000-22,000 crore order inflow
items.quote: As we enter Financial Year 2027, considering the economic and geopolitical situation, we remain optimistic about the opportunities ahead and expect to grow our top lines in the range of 15% and strengthen the order book with the target of new wins by INR20,000 crores to INR22,000 crores approximately, while continuing to remain selective and disciplined in our project bidding approach.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance INR300-350 crore
items.quote: As far as capital investment is concerned, it will be INR300 crores to INR350 crores, but about the return of Indus, Anand and Ankit will tell you.

items.statement: Order book INR26,470 crore as of date; bids worth INR13,500 crore yet to be opened

items.statement: Three main steel suppliers: Tata, JSW, Arcelor Mittal; supplies now normal but prices up 20%+ due to MIP

items.statement: No slowdown in PEB demand; strong inquiries from warehousing, gigafactory, data centre sectors

items.statement: Export revenue grew 156% year-on-year to INR165.6 crores in FY26; export volume 7,045 tons out of 73,000 tons total

items.statement: Net working capital at 39 days as of March 31, 2026 vs 33 days a year ago

items.statement: Employee strength: 440 white-collar in Phenix, 150-160 in Proflex; 1,600 workers across both plants

items.statement: Phenix volume growth target: 72,000 to 85,000-90,000 tons (20-25% growth); Proflex: 17 to 17.25 lakh sqm

items.statement: Near-term challenges: Iran conflict impact on margins and execution delays; labor constraints in Q1; monsoon in Q2; H2 historically stronger

items.statement: Minimum Import Price (MIP) on steel linked to dollar and freight causing domestic steel price hikes

items.statement: FY27 volume target of 7,000-8,000 MVA; FY28 volume target of more than 10,000 MVA

items.quote: So, this year we are hopeful that at least we should be touching 15% to 20% somewhere in between that is our faith in this.

items.quote: Grid modernization, renewable energy build-out, the rapid expansion of data centers driven by artificial intelligence adoption and a broader rise in the per capita electricity consumption are structural demand drivers that we believe these will sustain the transformer demand for at least next five to seven years, if not more.

items.statement: BESS seen as potential next game-changer like IDT; already executing BESS orders; substantial potential seen

items.quote: Obviously the orders that were already taken before this impact came in and those some of them as I said are firm priced orders. They are having some impact because as I mentioned not all commodity or material can be secured at the time of securing our transformer order.

items.statement: Company holding cash reserves with no current deployment plan

items.statement: Revenue remained subdued due to softer industry conditions and seasonal moderation in advertiser activity
items.quote: While revenue performance continued to remain subdued due to softer industry conditions, our efforts towards optimizing expenses and enhancing operational efficiencies supported in improving our margins and profitability during the quarter.

items.statement: Online and retail to constitute 75-85% of top line and bottom line going forward
items.quote: So th e online play with the retail play would be constituting at least 75 to 85% of our top line and bottom line as we move forward

items.statement: 22 new stores to be funded from IPO proceeds

items.quote: We have a total of 22 outlets, out of which 14 are New Balance exclusive brand outlets, and 8 are our Sneaker multi-brand stores.

items.quote: I would say that, yes, with 1 or 2% here and there. I believe the PAT margin was 15.5%. As we move forward, the top line will increase.

items.statement: Retail and e-commerce gross margins 54%+; B2B gross margin ~50%

items.statement: Margin differential between brands is 2-5%
items.quote: As I said, these guys are stopping me from giving you the differential. It is a couple of points here and there. So, let's say 2 to 5%.

items.quote: Through marketplace channels, roughly 20,000 plus PIN codes, our products are available to consumers, where we are in partnership with Myntra, Tata CLiQ, Tata CLiQ Luxury, Flipkart, Amazon, and everybody.

items.statement: Former CEO resigned for better opportunity; no replacement planned; procurement now overseen by family member with existing team in place
items.quote: No. I mean, no known reason to me. What was known is what was disclosed. He found a better opportunity, he moved on. That is what we know. And we don't intend to get a new CEO.

items.statement: Aspirational EBITDA margin 8% but realistic 6-6.5% in normal times; current gross margin ~24% target after price pass-through; lighting gross margin currently ~15% targeting 18-19% in 2-3 months
items.quote: Aspirational would be higher than that. 6%, 6.5% is definitely achievable. Aspirational would be closer to 8%, but when I say 8%, I also say that in the context of your question being aspirational.

items.statement: Chinese pricing remains a mystery; irrational competition seen in lighting segment; INR depreciation makes imports more expensive but China continues to offer lower rates
items.quote: We are not really able to logically work out how it is that they go on kind of offering lower rates to grab business. So Chinese pricing is somewhat of a mystery, I think, definitely to us and a lot of other Indian industry at large.

items.statement: Two-thirds of customers on quarterly price settlement (one quarter lag), one-third on monthly basis; price increases of 10-18% being negotiated
items.quote: With about maybe two-thirds of our customers it is on a quarterly basis. So, the pricing of Jan, Feb, March, for example, is applicable on the April, May, June price settlement. Therefore, there is a lag of a quarter.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation and war in Middle East causing supply chain disruptions, raw material cost spikes, and currency depreciation; minimum wage in Uttar Pradesh increased 26% effective April 2026
items.quote: Further, you would also have read that minimum wage has been revised upwards sharply in Uttar Pradesh resulting in an effective increase of 26% in April versus March. This was done on 14th April 2026 with effect from 1st April 2026.

items.statement: Management expects CX center utilization to exceed 91% by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: And the utilization levels as it stood on 31st of March was almost 83% and based on the business and books that we see, it is expected to move beyond 91% by the time we end the Quarter 1.

items.statement: Digital video studio investment approved at INR 11 crores for facilities, IT and real estate
items.quote: The investment in the digital video studio is already in the public domain. It is INR 11 crores.

items.statement: CX center capacity expanded by almost 50% with utilization at 83% as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: The second one was that we had expanded our infrastructure for the customer experience center. Now, we increased by almost 50%. And the utilization levels as it stood on 31st of March was almost 83%

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved from 13.5% to 15.5% in FY26
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 31.6% to almost INR 55 crores. And in terms of margins, it improved from almost 13.5% to around 15.5%.

items.statement: Revenue seasonality pattern: 40% in first half, 60% in second half driven by festival season and budget exhaustion
items.quote: Typically, 40% of revenue is in the first half and 60% percent is in the second half, and the reason for that is not difficult to fathom. Budgets get, let us say, assembled or determined in Q1 and then we hit the monsoon.

items.statement: Revenue mix approximately 44-45% communications, 25% research, 30% analytics based on standalone entity financials
items.quote: If one was to go with that caveat, and if one was to go with those individual standalone financials, then I would say that almost 44% to 45% of the top line of the income comes from the communication piece, a one-fourth comes from the research piece, and almost 30% thereabouts comes from the analytics piece.

items.statement: Multi-service client revenue share increased to 25-30% of total income from less than 5% previously
items.quote: And clients once they engage with you, they are quite happy to engage with you on other services as well. Why would they go elsewhere? It is from that point of view I think where we had maybe less than 5% of multi-service offerings to a particular client, I think we are at 25%-30% now.

items.statement: 5-year revenue CAGR of 14% from FY21 to FY26, outpacing Sensex (7.6%) and nominal GDP (8-9%)
items.quote: Therefore, if we were to look back, starting from FY21, and going up all the way to FY26, the total income for the company grew at a CAGR of almost 14%.

items.statement: Hired over 600 people in last 12-14 months; employee cost growth managed through muted increments, apprentice hiring, and superannuation exits
items.quote: We have hired over 600 people over the last 12-to 14 months.

items.statement: Positioned as independent homegrown player with speed and relevance advantages over MNC peers undergoing restructuring
items.quote: We are in a quadrant of one. We are on our own trip. We have built capabilities. We believe in this market. I do not write a single e-mail to New York or London or Tokyo to get approvals for anything.

items.statement: AI viewed as productivity tool embedded across workflows; not a displacement threat; 15 AI tools in use in communications alone
items.quote: AI is our tool. I mean, I have 15 in the communication piece only. I think there are 15 tools that are currently in use.

items.statement: Balance sheet remains zero-debt with healthy free cash flow generation
items.quote: The balance sheet continues to remain strong with a zero-debt position and healthy free cash flow generation.

items.statement: Consulting and video studio personnel investments in single-digit crores
items.quote: It is a very measured, Madhur. To answer your question, these are in single-digit crores. They are not large numbers.

items.statement: Capital allocation to remain measured; shareholder returns to be addressed at appropriate time
items.quote: We will not deploy it foolishly. Just because there is cash does not mean we need to go out and spend it. It will be done in a measured way only.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target 70-100% growth with similar profitability; long-term vision INR1,000 cr revenue by 2030 at 12-13% PAT margin
items.quote: I would like to give an outlook for FY27, which approximately I am expecting a target of 70% to 100% revenue growth, we have taken a minimum. And profit margins will also remain with similar profitability.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR300 cr minimum, Q1 revenue expected INR65-70 cr
items.quote: I am expecting my outlook for 2027 is INR300 crores. That is not going below INR300 crores, this is going to be above INR300 crores.

items.statement: AkikoPay FY27 revenue expected INR50-100 cr, Q1 INR4-5 cr
items.quote: From AkikoPay, I am expecting revenue in the first quarter because AkikoPay is properly indulged with our core business. If seen, I am expecting AkikoPay revenue of INR50 crores to INR100 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Loan business target INR1,000 cr unsecured book by FY27 end from current INR320 cr
items.quote: By FY27, my target is INR1,000 crores of unsecured book. So, the INR400 crores is to be taken to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: AkikoPay customer targets: 5 lakh by Sep 30, 1 million by Dec 31
items.quote: I am expecting 5 lakh customers by 30th of September and 1 million customers till 31st December.

items.statement: Q4 margin pressure due to branch expansion, tech investment, Dubai geopolitical issues; FY27 PAT margin guided 9-11%
items.quote: If we look at short-term profitability, margins could have been even stronger, but we have consciously invested to build future operating leverage for long-term scale. And some of our margin pressure has come in Dubai operations, there has b een temporary margin pressure due to the current geopolitical situation

items.statement: AkikoPay margins expected to improve to 12-13% via cross-sell; Q1 visibility, full scale Q2-Q3
items.quote: Yes, those margins will improve a lot. We can reach up to 12% to 13%. I am saying that those margins will improve a lot with cross-sales and all engagements.

items.statement: Monthly credit card disbursement 16,000+; monthly loan disbursement run rate INR400 cr+; annualized book INR5,000 cr
items.quote: Currently, we have reached a monthly disbursement run rate of INR400 crores+, which if we count annually, our book has become INR5,000 crores as of today.

items.statement: Unsecured loan book INR320 cr, secured INR80 cr; 80-20 split to remain
items.quote: Unsecured book is INR320 crores, rest is secured book.

items.statement: Branch expansion to 16 branches across India; technology infrastructure investment; AkikoPay development
items.quote: We have worked aggressively on branch infrastructure, technology systems, and Akiko's ecosystem, so that long-term sustainable growth can be built.

items.statement: Workforce 900+ (employees + channel partners); 16 branches across major cities; digital conversion 10% vs 60-80% with physical presence
items.quote: Reflecting this scale-up, our total combined workforce, including employees and channel partners, has now crossed 900+, which is a very strong growth compared to last year.

items.statement: 70% digital sourcing; 60% digital leads fulfilled by ground team, 40% from channel partners; AkikoPay integrating credit cards, loans, insurance, travel, UPI, AI tools
items.quote: Digitally, we are acquiring around 60% of the business. I mean, digital leads come then it goes to our ground, goes to our employees, they close the fulfilment. 40% business comes from our channel partners like builders, CAs, doctors and other co-channel partners.

items.statement: 25 million customer database; AkikoPay 57,000 downloads, 20% active users; targeting employees to drive 3,000-4,000 daily downloads
items.quote: Along with that, we have a database of 25 million customer base over the past years. So we will market them with nominal cost.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost INR10-15 vs INR250 for Paytm/PhonePe/CRED due to consent-based marketing to existing database
items.quote: Where Paytm, PhonePe or CRED spends around INR250 to acquire a customer, there our cost comes to INR10 to INR15. Because we are not marketing randomly.

items.statement: AkikoPay iOS launch delayed by compliance; now cleared, expected live this month; IRDAI license applied for insurance/mutual funds by August
items.quote: AkikoPay has not been integrated in Apple yet because there were some compliance issues. All those compliance issues have been

items.statement: FY26 receivable days decreased; cash flow from operations INR5 cr; unsecured focus avoids 2-3 month disbursement delays of secured loans
items.quote: FY26 receivable days have decreased and secondly, given your growth, even cash flow from operations has been reduced to INR5 crores.

items.statement: No fund-raising; completed integrations without external investment; building balance sheet without leverage
items.quote: Today we have completed almost all our integrations without any investment, without any fund-raising. And after that also we are at a good profitable margin and going towards scalability.

items.statement: Founder Ankur Gaba to take MD/CEO role in next 1-2 months; employee count 486 (up from 326), channel partners 430 (up from 100)
items.quote: Yes, 100%. Most likely in the next one or two months. I have already spoken with my management. They did agreed. So, we'll take a -- we'll take a decision very soon and in the next quarter, you will see me as an

items.statement: Q4 revenue INR57.7 cr (+48% YoY), EBITDA INR7.9 cr, PAT +30% YoY; FY26 revenue INR172.6 cr vs INR150 cr vision, PAT margin 10.3%
items.quote: In Q4, our revenue from operations has been INR57.7 crores, which is a 48% year-on-year growth. And EBITDA is INR7.9 crores. And PAT approximately has grown by 30%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue 126% growth, EBITDA 117% growth, PAT 120% growth; EPS doubled from 7.56 to 14.3
items.quote: And there has been a growth of 126% in revenue. And EBITDA has also grown by 117%. And PAT has also grown by 120%.

items.statement: Dubai revenue dropped from INR2-2.5 cr peak to INR50 lakh in Feb, recovered to INR1 cr in April, targeting INR1.25 cr in May; geopolitical risk around Iran region
items.quote: some of our margin pressure has come in Dubai operations, there has b een temporary margin pressure due to the current geopolitical situation, as you all know, around the Iran region

items.statement: AkikoPay iOS compliance risk resolved; Google Play Store download count fluctuation (50k to 10k display) being investigated
items.quote: Now compliance has also been completed, so most likely within this month, everything will be live.

items.statement: AkikoPay 1% cashback strategy sustainable for 1 year with 1.8% MDR and zero acquisition cost; 10-12% users opt for full KYC (2 lakh limit)
items.quote: Sir, this sustainability for next one year will be live because right now we are getting around 1.8% MDR and we are not putting any expense to acquire customer.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR330-350 crore standalone
items.quote: So, overall, we are anticipating we should be closing somewhere between INR330 crores to INR335 crores to INR350 crores.

items.statement: FY27 gross margin target minimum 15%
items.quote: we are anticipating that that should improve to 15% at a minimum.

items.statement: Flux-cored wire FY27 revenue expectation INR20 crore
items.quote: this year we are expecting somewhere if the industry improves and we see the demand again rising, so somewhere between INR20 odd crores is what we are expecting the flux-cored wire should contribute in this financial year.

items.statement: ERC business to start July, FY27 revenue INR30-35 crore
items.quote: that business will give us a revenue of on a annual basis almost like INR50 crores. So, even if we start somewhere in the month of July, so we expect at least between INR30 crores to INR35 crores coming from ERC business.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin 12.8%, down from 14.6%
items.quote: However, I can see that our gross margins dipped from 14.6% to 12.8% in this financial year.

items.statement: Trading margins very low, manufacturing margins higher
items.quote: Trading is something which we are doing it whenever -- because we try and take benefit of bulk procurement and we trade at relatively very low margins.

items.statement: ERC gross margin 25-28%
items.quote: ERC, the gross margins are relatively healthy, somewhere between 25% to 28% odd is the gross margin there.

items.statement: FY26 manufacturing 73%, trading 27% vs 67/33 last year
items.quote: The mix between manufacturing and trading this year is approximately 67% gross from manufacturing -- sorry 73% gross from manufacturing and 27% gross from trading, against 67% and 33% of last year.

items.statement: FY27 trading share expected below 20%
items.quote: In FY27, we are seeing -- because our -- the growth will come from the manufacturing segment, what we are projecting for this financial year. So, there's a -- it will drop down to less than 20%, the trading sales.

items.statement: Installed capacity: electrodes 10,600 MT, MIG wire 10,600 MT, flux-cored 2,500 MT
items.quote: Our installed production capacity currently stands at 10,600 metric tons for electrodes, 10,600 metric tons for MIG wire across West Bengal and Haryana facilities, and 2,500 metric tons for flux-cored wire.

items.statement: Flux-cored utilisation ~15% in FY26, peak revenue INR30 crore at 100%
items.quote: if you see the split, like last year flux wire has contributed nearly INR4 crores plus to the top line. So, when we see in terms of capacity utilization, it was at almost I think say 15%. Okay, and this year, obviously, whatever initial challenges were there, so that we have been able to overcome. And now we see this year should be, as I had mentioned in my earlier call, that on an optimum level a

items.statement: Debottlenecking and automation to improve throughput and utilisation
items.quote: We have also undertaken ongoing debottlenecking and automation initiatives across our manufacturing facilities, aimed at im proving throughput, operational efficiency, and capacity utilization

items.statement: Operational efficiency capex can push electrode capacity beyond 100% utilisation
items.quote: So, 85%, we had in fact mentioned that we have invested in capex for improving the operational efficiency. So, with the improvement in the operational efficiency, we can even cross your -- the capacity for electrodes.

items.statement: H2 FY26 sales impacted by war in last 15 days of March
items.quote: in the month of March, because of the war, so in the last 15 days, we actually basically saw an impact in terms of turnover.

items.statement: Direct wagon builder demand seeing resistance, dealer network stable
items.quote: We are basically seeing some pressure here, but as far as like your -- when it comes through dealer distribution network, so that business is not impacted so much. But when it comes to direct supplies to wagon builders, wagon manufacturers, there we are seeing a bit of resistance.

items.statement: Significant reduction in short-term borrowings strengthened balance sheet
items.quote: Another important achievement during FY26 was the significant red uction in short -term borrowings, which has further strengthened our balance sheet and liquidity position, providing greater financial flexibility for future growth initiatives

items.statement: Sales mix ~50-55% dealer distribution, 45-50% direct B2B
items.quote: See, it's a mix of like as I said B2B and B2C. The mix is somewhere between 50% -- 55% is from dealer distribution or it's other way to -- from direct to direct end consumers. So, you can say 45/55, somewhere -- sometime it is 50/50.

items.statement: Direct Railways contribution low 5-10%
items.quote: See, we are as government, non-government, largely our sales is to either wagon manufacturers who are in turn supplying to Railways, but direct Railways, like the contribution is low. It may be 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Invested INR1.8-1.9 crore in associate HM Power (14-15% stake) for bank capital requirement
items.quote: So, if you look at what is the quantum of that related party transaction in terms of because there's a investment which has been made in another company by the name HM Power, which is our associate company. So, the investment is I think less than INR1 crore. I think INR1.8 crores or INR1.9 crores is only the amount which has been invested in that company.

items.statement: HM Power associate FY27 revenue expected INR200 crore, Classic owns 14-15%
items.quote: Out of that company, in this current financial year, we are expecting a revenue of INR200 crores.

items.statement: Margin guidance contingent on war situation normalising
items.quote: Again, it'll all depend how the global situation, how the global war -- the war between U.S. and Iran subsides or where it leads to, because every day we see something new coming up. So, I think everything has a positive or a negative impact because of the global situation.

items.statement: Commitment to quarterly business updates and announcements
items.quote: Otherwise, definitely we'll share at least quarter-on-quarter what is our revenue growth, what we had shared in Q3, we will continue doing that.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 25-30% minimum with similar margins
items.quote: We aim to grow by 25% to 30% minimum in FY '27 with similar margins.

items.statement: PAT margin expected around 14% in FY27
items.quote: See we will be maintaining the PAT of around 14% approximately.

items.statement: INR 25 crores capex incurred in FY26
items.quote: During the year, we incurred INR25 crores in capital expenditure, reflecting our continuous investment in infrastructure and capabilities.

items.statement: IPO proceeds reallocation of INR 10 crores to nutraceutical facility expansion
items.quote: The board has approved a reallocation of INR 10 crores, primarily from surplus amounts across the veterinary facility , home care, and cosmetic divisions , towards the enhanced construction cost for the nutraceutical CDMO facility.

items.statement: New 75,000 sq ft facility expected operational by July-August 2026, increasing installed capacity 2.5x
items.quote: Our most significant ongoing initiative is the development of a new facility , approximately 75,000 square feet of ground plus four floor structure , expected to become operational by or August 2026. Upon commissioning, this expansion is anticipated to increase our overall installed capacity by approximately 2.5 times the existing

items.statement: Pet care capacity to reach 25 tons/month in 2-3 months; extrusion line upgrade from 100-150 kg/hr to 1000 kg/hr ordered
items.quote: In pet care, our current output stands at around 16 to 18 tons per month with a near term capacity expected to reach to 25 tons per month within the next two to three months. We have also ordered a high-capacity pet food extrusion line, upgrading from our 100-150 kg per hour to 1000 kg per hour to support the long term growth demand.

items.statement: Beverage canning facility planned at 10,000 bottles/hour with Tetra pack line booked
items.quote: We are building out a canning facility and a carbonated beverage line with a Tetra pack line already booked. Plan ned installed capacity is approximately 10,000 bottles per hour.

items.statement: Client base of 718+ with 98% retention rate
items.quote: On the client front, we have served a base of 718 plus clients with a retention rate of 98% , reflecting the strength of our long term relationships and consistency of product quality.

items.statement: New clients added including Nykaa, Khandelwal Labs, Aristo
items.quote: We have good orders, we have a good client base. We have started a lot of new companies are rolled in with good names like Nykaa, Khandelwal Labs. There are many good names that have joined. Aristo is there.

items.statement: Protein and snack bar demand more than doubled
items.quote: The protein and snack bar line sub segment also witnessed a strong growth with demand more than doubling.

items.statement: Export growth at 10-15% annually; international markets to be increasingly meaningful
items.quote: Export growth continues at 10% to 15% annually and we expect international markets to be an increasingly meaningful contributor going forward.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 72 bps to 20.3%; PAT margin expanded 129 bps to 14%
items.quote: With full year EBITDA margin expanding by 72 bps to 20.3%. PAT stood at around INR10.5 crores for H2 FY '26 u p by 38% year-on-year, bringing full year FY PAT to INR20.5 crores with full year PAT margin expanding by 129 bps points to 14%.

items.statement: Gross margin dip in H2 due to packaging and raw material cost increases with lag in pass-through
items.quote: As I said, lastly, if you see the couple of months, yes due to the war crisis, there has been a rise in the packaging material, laminates , and all. So there , see we follow cost plus basis only, but there is always going to be a lag, actually.

items.statement: Segment gross margins: nutra 30-35%, cosmetic 40%+, veterinary/ayurvedic 30-35%
items.quote: Gross margin is approximately 30% to 35% in nutra. Then in cosmetic also it's slightly higher better, it may be around 40% plus. And then veterinary ayurvedic and this is around 30% to 35% sir.

items.statement: Cost-plus pricing model; raw material cost increases passed to customers with lag
items.quote: See yeah, it is passed to them sir. There can be a little bit lag, but it is passed to them. As if we don't do much whey protein now because whey protein the market is very price oriented and there is a lot of less margin into it.

items.statement: Packaging material, laminates, solvents (IPA), coating materials costs increased 2-3% gradually
items.quote: No both. RM also is there because if you see the coating materials like solvents which are there, IPA and all it increased a lot. So that was there, but again it is now on the you know it is coming down to normal and inventory we have increased.

items.statement: Nutra revenue INR 131 cr (40.3% YoY), cosmetic INR 7.4 cr (15.8% YoY), ayurvedic INR 6.1 cr (88.9% YoY), other INR 1.4 cr (18.7% YoY)
items.quote: Segment-wise, nutraceuticals contributed around INR131 crores up to 40.3% year -on-year growth, cosmetics around INR7.4 crores which is 15.8% year -on-year growth. Ayurvedic products contributed around INR6.1 crores up by 88.9% year -on-year growth. The other segment comprising veterinary and home care reported INR1.4 crores reflecting 18.7% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute 30-40% of revenue; Novus and Octavius are top clients
items.quote: Yeah, so our top 10, 20 clients are giving us approximately 30% to 40% revenue. There are many clients which are there and these clients are coming in the top.

items.statement: Novus supplies raw materials, helping reduce payable days and working capital
items.quote: Novus is no doubt they are supplying few of the goods raw materials for themselves, but we have drastically reduced them. As evident in the reduced cycle in the payables. So it has reduced because of them only, thanks to Novus.

items.statement: FY26 cash conversion cycle 64 days; debtor days 84 (from 113), inventory days 99 (from 112), payable days improved from 248 to 119
items.quote: FY26 cash conversion cycle stood at 64 days with debtor days improving to 84 days from 113 in FY '25. Inventory days also improved to 99 days from 112 days in FY '25 and payable days improving from 119 days from 248 days in FY '25.

items.statement: No debt planned; sufficient funds from IPO proceeds and internal accruals for next 2-3 years
items.quote: See right now, we have sufficed our money for which is the IPO proceedings we have done. So right now we don't look forward for debt and everything, we don't require also.

items.statement: INR 13.84 crores of IPO proceeds utilized for capex as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: As of March 31, 2026, INR 13.84 crores of the IPO proceeds allocated for capex have been utilized.

items.statement: Regulatory approvals received for Tanzania and Nigeria; Kenya under consideration; NSF second audit completed May 5
items.quote: On the export front, we have received regulatory approvals for Tanzania and Nigeria, with Kenya currently under consideration. We have also established a new office in the UAE focused on high-margin opportunities in this region.

items.statement: Export contribution 15-20% currently; targeting 5-7% annual increase in export quantum
items.quote: So right now maybe we are doing around 15% to 20%. But year on year we can increase 5% to 7% that way for the export quantum.

items.statement: Employee cost up 31% in H2 FY26 vs H1 FY26 due to new hires for RTD/nutra units and October salary increments
items.quote: Coming to employee expense, there was an addition to the workforce for the upcoming RTD and nutraceutical units. As we speak, the additional workforce is under training and there was an annual salary increment for the employees in the month of October, resulting in a significant increase in employee cost by 31% in H2 FY '26 as compared to H1 FY '26.

items.statement: ROE 30%, asset turnover 5.3x in FY26
items.quote: Return on equity stood at 30%, reflecting efficient capital allocation. Asset turnover stood at 5.3x reflecting strong operational productivity.

items.statement: Capacity utilization varies by segment: nutra ~72%, cosmetic ~55%, pet supplement ~75%; filling new capacity will take time
items.quote: See, it's approximately - all different segments have different utilizations. See , first of all, utilization is not a big thing , ma'am, because we have grown that . As I have consistently emphasized, we prefer steady growth in the machinery division. We want to avoid making large upfront investments before we have secured clients. So right now, nutraceutical is somewhere around 72% utilization,

items.statement: Expects 25-30% revenue growth over next 3-5 years driven by new factories and products
items.quote: So, you can expect at least 25% to 30% growth in the next three to five years with these new factories coming and new products coming up.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR271 crores, mostly for execution in FY27
items.quote: And the best part is we have a very strong order book today of INR271 crores, which is going to be executed mostly in the year 2027.

items.statement: Planned INR20 crores for Karachiya GIS factory, INR19 crores for Odisha unit from IPO proceeds
items.quote: Overall, we have planned for INR20 crores to be placed in Karachiya GIS factory in Baroda, second unit of INR19 crores in Odisha, and the other funds were to be utilized for short-term borrowings.

items.statement: GIS manufacturing facility at Vadodara to be inaugurated in September 2026
items.quote: We are going to , we have plans to inaugurate as per our RHP/DRHP filing, September 2026, and we are on our way to complete that project and will be inviting all of you in the month of -- for GIS manufacturing inauguration.

items.statement: Odisha facility timeline accelerated from May 2027 to October 2026 via rented facility
items.quote: So, we are on our way and we are cutting down, shortening our timeline from May 2027 to October 2026. So, we will be able to contribute to Eastern India eight to nine months earlier than what was originally planned after IPO fund.

items.statement: GIS factory adds INR200 crores revenue potential; Odisha factory adds INR100 crores when fully operational
items.quote: so I can say we can add another INR200 crores revenue actually when we start full-fledged and we start operating fully with the present capex. And Odisha, we are expecting to add another INR100 crores in terms of sales revenue when the Odisha facility will be fully operative

items.statement: Peak power demand projected to reach 335 GW by FY2030, 60% higher than 2023 estimates
items.quote: And it is projected by FY 2030 to reach 335 gigawatt, which is 60% higher than what was expected in 2023.

items.statement: Data center boom expected; India has only 40-60 data centers vs 3,500-4,000 in USA despite 4x population
items.quote: In the USA, if you see, I was listening a year before, there were 3,500 to 4,000 data centers across the US with a population of you can say, one-third or one-fourth of India, while India has hardly 40, 50, or 60 data centers across India with a population four times than the USA.

items.statement: FY26 exports INR31 crores; targets 20-25% of manufacturing revenue from exports going forward
items.quote: Last year, you know, we have done almost INR31 crores export out of the complete manufacturing you can say, revenue, and going forward, we expect that at least 20% to 25% of the revenue comes from our export business.

items.statement: Won INR45.4 crores compact substation order for Reliance AI data center in Jamnagar
items.quote: One of the huge wins for us is INR45.4 crores MV block compact substation order, which is for the AI factory of Reliance Data Center in Jamnagar.

items.statement: Secured INR84 crores RDSS EPC order from PGVCL to supply RMUs and underground network
items.quote: We have got a very good order from PGVCL. It is again for the RDSS project, INR84 crores.

items.statement: ZESCO Zambia trial order INR10.62 crores; expects larger follow-on orders and refurbishment unit setup
items.quote: ZESCO Limited successfully executed INR10.62 crores order. You know the story behind this? They were in a search of Ring Main Units and compact substations from India.

items.statement: Working capital reduced from INR33 crores to INR17 crores; working capital cycle at 73 days in FY26
items.quote: You know, our working capital requirement was INR33 crores last year, and it has reduced to INR17 crores this year. It is because we could push those INR15 crores into this short-term repayment of short-term borrowings.

items.statement: Plans to raise INR10-13 crores for working capital to fund growth; bank renewal due September
items.quote: So, just to cater to this additional working capital requirement for next six months, we thought that we should go for this raising of INR10 crores to INR12 crores or INR13 crores, which is going to be handy for us in executing the projects on hand in a faster manner.

items.statement: Coex volumes moderated in FY26 due to temporary slowdown in refrigerator production from early monsoon

items.quote: Out of INR140 crores, we have done around INR55 crores to INR60 crores to date. And in this console thing, another INR5 crores or something we have received.

items.statement: Receivables split approximately 60% NHAI, 40% state government

items.statement: NHAI introduced running account basis for price escalation calculations to help contractors
items.quote: Now they have introduced something , like they have instructed all the regional offices to calculate the escalations on a running account basis, so that it will be easier for the contractors.

items.statement: Maximum technical capacity INR400-500 crore per order; currently targeting INR100 crore minimum orders
items.quote: The maximum is around INR400 crores to INR500 crores , and the minimum, we are targeting at INR100 crores or something.

items.statement: May consider bill discounting if cash crunch arises; confident of equity raise and warrant exercise to reduce debt
items.quote: If we at all have to face that cash crunch at all, we'll make sure that the receivables are there within this cycle of what we are maintaining. And also, we might go for discounting of debtors, which we have not done till now.

items.statement: Recruited special tendering team in last 2 months to bid on 100+ tenders for higher win probability
items.quote: So, what we have decided is instead of bidding for 10 tenders and getting 2 tenders, we have decided to go bid for 100 tenders so that the probability will be much higher. So, we have recruited a special team in the last 2 months so that they keep on working on all the tenders that are positive for us.

items.statement: Trade payables flat at INR20 crore despite 4x revenue growth from INR115 crore to INR420 crore over 3 years
items.quote: In financial year '25, our trade payable was standing somewhere INR16 crores, where we had a top line of INR272 crores. In financial year '26, we're having a top line of INR420 crores, stand- alone and the trade payable stand -alone, I'm talking to you, is around INR20 crores, sir.

items.statement: NHAI and state officials discussing VG30 bitumen substitution for VG40 to ease supply constraints
items.quote: VG40 is a problematic thing. So, what the NHAI and other state officials are now on the talks to get it done with VG30 itself. VG30 and VG40 are not much of a difference. So, they are planning to have the conditions not restricted to VG40 and where they may implement VG30.

items.statement: No political party linkages; rumors stem from brother-in-law being actor and new CM Vijay also being actor
items.quote: I don't have any link with any political parties except for two days. One day, I'll vote for the State election, one day for the Central election. Apart from that, I don't have any link with anyone. Apart from that, any other thing, see, there is a rumour going on in because my brother- in-law is a leading actor in the Tamil industry.
