name: E To E Transportation Infrastructure Limited

items.statement: Management targets 45-50% revenue CAGR for FY27 with similar profitability and margin levels as FY26
items.quote: The management is positive towards keeping the momentum on the same CAGR of 45% to 50%, maintaining the same profitability and t he margin levels

items.statement: Management targets INR1,000 crore new order inflows in FY27, with INR350 crore already secured in first 45 days
items.quote: Throughout the year we are targeting somewhere around taking our this year itself the new orders this year itself around INR1,000 crores on this year itself.

items.statement: Executable order book including L1 position stands at INR860 crore plus GST (over INR1,000 crore including GST) as of call date
items.quote: As of now, our executable order book including L1 position stands at approximately INR860 crores plus GST, which is more than INR1,000 crores including if we include the GST.

items.statement: INR350 crore new orders secured in first 45 days of FY27, including INR200 crore+ composite signaling and electrification order from South Central Railway
items.quote: Within the first 45 days of FY27 itself, we have already secured significant order wins and L1 positions across multiple railway signaling and infrastructure projects.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin decline of ~1% due to INR1.5 crore ESOP expense, INR0.5 crore NOVA expenses, and INR2 crore commodity timing impact; medium-term margin trajectory positive
items.quote: There were very few specific factors during FY26, which have contributed towards marginally lowering the total overall EBITDA margins. And most of them are transitional or timing related rather than any structural in nature.

items.statement: INR15 crore capex planned for NOVA in FY27 funded through internal accruals
items.quote: There is an investment plan of around INR15 crores this particular year to be made into Nova, and that will be basically through our accruals from e2E itself because it's a 100% owned subsidiary.

items.statement: NOVA received CCA approval from RDSO for Kavach development on May 15, 2026; field trial orders expected by end of H1 FY27, revenue recognition from FY28 Q1
items.quote: On 15th of May 2026, NOVA received CCA Approval from RDSO for Kavach development. This is a major strategic milestone for the organization. With this approval, NOVA is now eligible to submit its prototypes for approval while being eligible to receive field trial orders under the Kavach ecosystem.

items.statement: NOVA developing additional safety-critical railway applications beyond Kavach with Tata Elxsi; product announcements expected in coming months
items.quote: NOVA is actively right now working in developing few of the safety-critical applications. We will be in a position to announce the exact products in few months of time once we have started and properly registered in the right forums and the authorities.

items.statement: FY26 receivables spike due to billing concentration in March from delayed bid-to-LOA conversions; INR90 crore collected in first 45 days of FY27; targeting operating cash flow neutral in FY27
items.quote: Collections have already started normalizing steadily in the Q1 FY27, and in last 45 days, we have collected more than INR90 crores in this cycle of the last two months' billing.

items.statement: Railway receivables debtor days at 60-70 days; unbilled revenue at 8.6% for FY26 (cumulative 34%); structural seasonality with H2 execution concentration
items.quote: Our debtor days in terms of railway receivables on the debtor basis, is around 60 to 70 days, and we get back the money.

items.statement: Adjusted debt-equity ratio at 0.68x and ROCE at ~17% in FY26; disciplined balance sheet management maintained despite 50%+ revenue growth
items.quote: If you see our adjusted debt-equity ratio stands at approximately 0.68, while our ROCE remains strong at around 17%.

items.statement: B2G (Indian Railways) provides scale; B2B improving cash conversion with faster receivable cycles and lower working capital intensity
items.quote: The B2G segment, which is primarily to the Indian Railways, continues to provide scale and participation in large national railway modernization programs. At the same time, the B2B business is helping improve the cash conversion efficiency through faster receivable cycles and lower working capital intensity.

items.statement: Bid conversion ratio of 20-25% maintained; competitive moat from integrated system integration, engineering design (EDRC), and NOVA product capability vs standalone OEMs
items.quote: We have been maintaining a steady bid conversion ratio of around 20% to 25% over the years. And that is one of the massive moats which the company has because of the design capability which is an in-house design capability which we have, through our EDRC.

items.statement: Kavach TAM expanded from INR50,000 crore to INR1,50,000-2,00,000 crore due to government expanding scope to entire high-density network, 20,000+ locomotives, and high-speed rail
items.quote: Now you see that the government is with the success of the initial rollout of Kavach, the government have focused on rolling out Kavach for the entire high-density, high-utilized network plus also the other corridors. Also, the other corridors and the total 20,000 locomotives, which is in the cycle, plus we also have every year 300 to 500 locomotives being added in the system.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue target ~INR200 crore (40% of full year); quarterly run rate ~INR100 crore in H1 and INR160-170 crore in H2
items.quote: our proposal --our projection is H1 we should be around closing in around INR200 crores. So that's the guidance what we are trying to give. The rest will be building H2. Monthly is a little difficult to project, but it is more or less quarterly and the q uarterly run rate for -- for the H1 is around INR100 crores and for H2 it will be around INR160 crores to INR170

items.statement: O&M revenue target 5-6% of total revenue in FY27; contracts typically 5-15 years with PVC escalation clauses
items.quote: This year, this particular FY27, we are trying to at least get to around 5% to 6% of our revenues from the O&M business.

items.statement: Execution cycle typically 18-24 months (max 30 months); targeting improved H1/H2 split from 35/65 to 40/60 in FY27
items.quote: So generally execution cycle for our business is typically around 24, -- 18 to 24 months and some sometimes it gets extended to around maximum 30 months.

items.statement: Evaluating international opportunities in Southeast Asia, Middle East, Africa through design engineering and product verticals; cautious approach given geopolitical environment
items.quote: Alongside domestic growth, we are also carefully evaluating international opportunities, particularly through our design engineering and product verticals. We believe markets across Southeast Asia, Middle East, and Africa can create meaningful opportunitie s over the medium term. However, at the same time, given the current geopolitical environment globally, we remain cautious and calibrated in ou

items.statement: Labour management planned seasonally; summer working hours 6:30-11:30 and 16:00-19:00 with night shifts for emergencies; work more system integration than labour intensive
items.quote: Say, for example, for peak summer, our working hours generally happens from 6:30 to 11:30 and then we again start doing the work from 4:00 to 7:00. So even some point of time where it is allowed to do night working, we can also do with proper lighting and safety measures, we also do some night working in case of any kind of emergency or an expedited work requirement.

items.statement: PVC clauses protect against commodity inflation; FY26 impact from timing mismatch between March billing concentration and PVC recovery; better billing distribution in FY27 to capture full escalation benefit
items.quote: Though, while most of our contracts contain PVC Clauses which protect us against commodity price fluctuations. The timing of this sudden increase and the year-end execution concentration did not actually allow the full impact of those escalations to be recovered wi thin the same financial

items.statement: Vision 2029: target INR1,000+ crore annual revenue with sustainable profitability through technology ownership, vertical integration, OEM capability, and recurring lifecycle revenues
items.quote: As we move towards Vision 2029, our ambition is very clear. We aim to build a resilient, innovation-led railway technology enterprise capable of crossing INR1,000 crore s in annual revenue while sustainably expanding profitability through technology ownership, vertical integration, OEM capability, and recurring life cycle revenues

items.statement: Order book of INR36-38 crores executable in FY27, mostly from in-building accessories, IBS, network accessories and services; EMS is a small portion
items.quote: Look, it is mostly from what you say, in-building accessories, IBS and network accessories, and our services business.

items.statement: EMS order book is currently a small portion of the total INR36-38 crore order book
items.quote: EMS is right now a small portion, yes.

items.statement: CCTV portfolio undergoing STQC approvals; expecting approval by end of Q1 FY27 after firmware change iterations
items.quote: So, I think, by the end of this quarter, we are expecting that we should get through.

items.statement: CCTV go-to-market ready; initial focus on North India which has 60-65% of surveillance market concentration
items.quote: Our first focus is going to be North India territory because that is where the surveillance market is about 60%-65% surveillance market is concentrated there.

items.statement: DAS business stalled in FY26 due to stalemate between mobile operators and neutral hosts on rentals; delays in Navi Mumbai Airport and Mumbai Metro projects
items.quote: There has been stalemate between what you say, mobile operators and neutral hosts pertaining to the rentals being charged for providing these services.

items.statement: DAS opportunity pipeline reviving with commissioning of Navi Mumbai and Noida Airport Phase I; future expansion phases expected to generate business by end of FY27
items.quote: So, there are going to be future phases which are going to come and maybe towards the end of this financial year, we can expect some business from the expansion side of it.

items.statement: Mumbai Metro revenue potential estimated at INR20-25 crores if operators decide to deploy directly; decision pending but could happen within FY27
items.quote: Revenue potential for Mumbai Metro will be around, I think, INR20 crores to INR25 crores.

items.statement: EMS business onboarded 6-7 customers across induction heaters, hobs, smart meters, power adapters, EV charging PCBs; expecting revenue in excess of INR5 crores in FY27 with potential to add more lines mid-year
items.quote: From the current setup that we have, we are expecting in this current financial year revenues in excess of INR5 crores from this line.

items.statement: Noida facility has 1 SMT line on one shift; infrastructure ready to expand to 4 SMT lines on 3 shifts (12x capacity); first priority for in-house DAS, repeater, CCTV products; unutilized capacity for third-party EMS
items.quote: Currently we are using one SMT line in one shift and we can expand it to four SMT lines in three shifts. So, 12-fold. That is all.

items.statement: Management confident of achieving INR500 crore revenue target by FY28; FY27 expected to beat FY25 revenue; no specific FY27 percentage growth guidance given
items.quote: I don't want to put a number to this right now. We are still evaluating things currently, but I am pretty sure on the number for next year, which is there INR500 crores, that target still stays and we are very much going to achieve that.

items.statement: Defense segment: repeater solutions trialled and accepted; interference mitigation solution in trials; repeater opportunity estimated at INR40-50 crores per annum; interference mitigation equally large
items.quote: For repeaters, I see there is opportunity of almost about INR40- INR50 crores opportunity size is there depending again on which all areas they go with and how soon they go with the solution.

items.statement: DAS slowdown also seen outside India due to war situation causing project delays
items.quote: There has been slowdown outside India as well, mostly pertaining to the war situation.

items.statement: Added one of India's leading telecom operators as new customer for RF repeater business; platform to expand into IBS accessories, network accessories and other telecom infrastructure products
items.quote: During the year, we added one of the India's leading telecom operators as a new customer and successfully commenced RF repeater business with them.

items.statement: Commercial launch of AI-powered video analytics platform AI EYE; CCTV portfolio in STQC approvals; Get Five Bars indoor connectivity solution in pilot deployments; developing network interference mitigation and mobile coverage solutions for
items.quote: On the product innovation front, we achieved an important milestone with the commercial launch of our AI-powered video analytics platform, AI EYE.

items.statement: Appointed as Digital Connectivity Rating Agency (DCRA) by TRAI creating scalable services-led revenue stream; 5G Site Implementation services commenced and contributing at early stage
items.quote: We are now an appointed Digital Connectivity Rating Agency or DCRA by TRAI, creating a scalable services-led revenue stream.

items.statement: Payments secure as Frog works with system integrators/neutral hosts; payments not dependent on disputes between neutral host and end clients like Mumbai Metro
items.quote: Our payments are not dependent on what happens - what transpire between them and, let's say, Mumbai Metro. Right? So, our payment remains secure.

items.statement: New TRAI DCRA regulation creates digital connectivity rating for buildings; Frog appointed as DCRA; framework expected to drive demand for in-building coverage solutions from building owners and operators
items.quote: And if you see this new TRAI regulation. using DCRA now there is regulation where the buildings are going to get digital certification.

items.statement: Structural change in FY26: services business transferred to 100% subsidiary Frog Services Private Limited; customers now place orders directly on Frog Services instead of routing through Frog Cellsat, creating consolidated vs standalone rev
items.quote: In last year, we did this structural change. We have transferred most of the business to be for services business to be done directly by Frog Services.

name: Krishna Defence and Allied Industries Limited

items.statement: Targets 30%+ revenue growth for next few years
items.quote: We aspire to grow at a rate about 30% plus for the next few years and this is how we are going to get there.

items.statement: Expects margin improvement in FY27 assuming product mix remains same
items.quote: Assuming the product mix remains the same, we'll see an update. Plus operation leverage kicks in, right? Operation leverage also kicks in. So that does help too.

items.statement: Order book INR1,034 million and tender pipeline INR2,210 million as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: As on 31 March, 2026, needless to reiterate, we had a very strong order book and a strong tender pipeline as well amounting to INR1,034 million and INR2,210 million respectively.

items.statement: Tender pipeline of INR220 crore expected to fructify in FY27
items.quote: This will be realized in FY27.

items.statement: Order inflow in FY26 was lower due to Operation Sindoor delaying orders by 4-5 months
items.quote: What changed is we had operation Sindoor in four or five months. The focus of the government was on immediate deployment that is there. So, whatever had to come between April and September, October all got pushed back for five months.

items.statement: Purchased 50,000 sq ft plot for capacity expansion; CapEx for Chennai and Halol land
items.quote: We purchased a joining shed, it's about 50,000 square feet plot for the capacity expansion that we are looking to do.

items.statement: JV with Vabo Composite requires INR4-5 crore investment from company side
items.quote: The funding required is about INR4 crores, INR5 crores only from our side. So which we can do from an internal. We don't have to plan or take a debt to be able to fund that.

items.statement: Doubled bulb bar capacity from 2,000-2,500 tons to 4,000-4,500 tons in April 2025
items.quote: We doubled our capacity from 2,000, 2,500 tons of bulb bar to about 4,000, 4,500 tons of Bulb Bar in April 2025.

items.statement: Current infrastructure can support INR400-500 crore revenue with modernization
items.quote: The infrastructure that we have, as I mentioned earlier, we can get to a INR400 crore to INR500 crore in the same infrastructure with some modernization, automation that we built inside.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 21.3% up 511 bps YoY; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 24.8% up 206 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of revenue for the year 2024, it was stood at 21.3% showing an increase of 511 basis point year-over-year.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by product mix shift to higher-margin armoured profiles and weld consumables
items.quote: One of the reasons for the specific higher margin throughout FY26 compared to FY25 is due to the product mix. So earlier we were only doing bulb bars, right? But now we have other products in an anvil, which is your armour steel profiles, your weld consumables, and a few other products that we are doing. There the margin percentage is higher.

items.statement: FY26 product mix: ~60% bulb bars, ~15% welding wires, ~15% armoured steel profiles, ~10% others
items.quote: About bulb bars, about close to 60%. The welding wires, about 15% odd that is there, HVF, the armoured steel profile, about 15% odd. And roughly around that, then others would be another 10%.

items.statement: Expects similar product mix for FY27
items.quote: It will be similar. Yes, you're right, sir.

items.statement: Top customer contributes ~35-40% of revenue but varies by shipyard order flow
items.quote: So about 40% of the revenue, 35% odd comes from one particular customer, but that keeps changing. So that's a shipyard for us, for a shipyard for us, and the rest follows accordingly.

items.statement: Certified supplier to all major Indian shipyards; next-gen corvette orders will flow to company
items.quote: Yeah, 100%, sir. Not some, we get whatever the requirement of the products that we are doing, we are certified for the product. That will, - - that part order will surely come to us.

items.statement: Received AS9100D aerospace certification and IRS certification for commercial shipbuilding
items.quote: A very key certification that we got is the AS9100D certification which is a mandatory quality certification for you to get into the aerospace particular components. We also got our IRS certification which qualifies us for commercial shipbuilding.

items.statement: Holds 20% stake in Conceptia (ship/submarine design) and 40% in Waveoptix (RF-optical modules)
items.quote: We also have a 20% stake in a design company called Conceptia which is into last 15 to 18 years has been into ship and submarine design and block design so on so forth. We also have a 40% stake that's an associate company in Waveoptix defence solution.

items.statement: Invested 47% in Taharabadkar Solutions for smart ammunition (DART) indigenization; product development 2-3 years
items.quote: It'll take about two to three years to successfully develop the product that is there. Post that, very high numbers that are there.

items.statement: Conceptia FY26 revenue ~INR80 crore, PAT ~INR5 crore, order book INR20-25 crore
items.quote: When we look at Conceptia, they did a revenue of about close to INR80-odd crores that is there with the PAT in the range of about close to INR5 crores is what they did. And their order book is in the range of about INR20 crores, INR25 crores that is per se.

items.statement: Waveoptix FY26 revenue ~INR22-23 crore, PAT ~INR5-5.5 crore, order book ~INR6 crore
items.quote: When it comes to Waveoptix, they've done a revenue of about close to INR22 crores or INR23 crore with a PAT margin about close to INR5 crores to INR5.5 crores for this financial year. And their order book, open order book position is about close to INR6 crores.

items.statement: Conceptia projects 20% growth, Waveoptix projects ~30% growth for FY27
items.quote: So these two companies also, both Conceptia and Waveoptix, as per their projection, they will also be growing; Conceptia at about 20%, and Waveoptix at about close to 30 odd%.

items.statement: Seeing raw material cost increases in steel and fuel but not substantial margin impact
items.quote: Yes, we are. So it's a global issue that is there. So how could we be insulated? There is going to be an uptake in terms of fuel costs, in steel prices, all of that. So that definitely, there is an uptake in that. There is going to be an increase in the raw material pricing, increase the conversion cost per se.

items.statement: Inventory dropped to INR163 crore at year-end due to timing; average inventory ~INR40 crore
items.quote: The inventory is just a cut off on that particular date. Our raw materials that were to come in February and March have come in first week of April that is there. But if you saw the average inventory holding that is there, Krishna Defence & Allied Industries Limited Q4 & FY26 Post Earnings Conference Call May 22, 2026 that was in the range of about INR40 odd crore rupees

items.statement: Cash balance north of INR100 crore including INR65 crore liquid reserves in long-term FDs
items.quote: Yeah, I couldn't unmute sorry. Yeah, yeah, that helps sir. So just trying to understand, so our cash balance is sitting at north of INR100 crore right now. Would that be fair to say? Manish Shah: Yes, you are right. In ball park, you are right.

items.statement: Bulb bar and weld consumables classified; not allowed to export
items.quote: The steels that we are doing for the Bulb bar, for the Navy or the weld consumable, these are all classified. So we are not allowed to export the same as we speak.

items.statement: AUV development with Navy/DRDO and NIO Goa ToT; Indian Navy earmarked ~$1 billion for autonomous underwater platforms
items.quote: The Navy has earmarked in budget about close to $1 billion on the autonomous or AUV space that is there.

items.statement: Expects to reach around 65% capacity utilization by end of current fiscal year (FY27)
items.quote: broadly we anticipate that by the end of the current fiscal year, we should reach around 65% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% export revenue share over next three years
items.quote: broadly we see that in next three years Neochem's target is that we should have 30-35% revenue coming from exports.

items.statement: Aims to bring trade receivables to around 120 days by H1 FY27 or latest by end of FY27
items.period: H1 FY27 or end of FY27
items.quote: we aim to bring it to a round 120 days, maybe by H1 FY27 or latest by the end of FY27.

items.statement: Believes sustainable margins are 35% gross, 18-20% EBITDA, 10-12% PAT for current product mix
items.quote: we believe these margins are sustainable for this kind of product mix and the industries that we currently cater to, around 35% gross margin, around 18% to 20% EBITDA margin, and around 10% to 12% PAT margin.

items.statement: Expects operating cash flow to normalize by current fiscal year-end (FY27)
items.quote: Broadly by the current fiscal year-end, it would be quite healthier than what it is today.

items.statement: No major planned capex over next 1.5-2 years; only minor equipment additions for formulations
items.quote: we will not require any major planned capex over the next one -and-a-half to two years. However, ours is a formulation -driven business wherein certain formulations may require a couple of equipment additions or some lab testing equipment, which is an ongoing requirement for any manufacturing company.

items.statement: Installed capacity 22,000 MTPA; utilization improved from 35% in FY24 to 53% in FY26 with 47% headroom
items.quote: Over the last few years, capacity utilization has steadily improved from approximately 35% in FY24 to 53% in FY26. As utilization levels continue to improve, we expect to benefit from stronger fixed cost absorption and operating leverage, supporting sustainable margin expansion over time.

items.statement: Delivered 26% volume growth and 32% value growth in FY26
items.quote: So we delivered exactly 26% volume growth year-on-year and 32% value growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 321 bps to 20.4% in FY26 driven by favorable product mix, higher utilization, operating leverage, cost discipline
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 321 basis points to 20.4% compared to 17.2% in the previous year. The improvement in profitability was driven by a combination of favorable product mix, higher capacity utilization, operating leverage benefits, and continued cost discipline across the business.

items.statement: Raw material cost remained broadly aligned with revenue growth; 30% of raw materials directly crude-linked; passed on price increases to customers during West Asia crisis
items.quote: Raw material cost remained broadly aligned with the revenue growth, reflecting a relatively stable input cost environment during the year.

items.statement: Shifted from 75% white-label in FY22 to >80% own-brand in FY26; targeting bio-based esters and silicones to contribute 55-60% of revenue in 2 years
items.quote: We would like these two categories to contribute around 55% to 60% of our total revenu e over the next two years.

items.statement: Textile share fell from 85% in FY25 to <75% in FY26; targets <50% in 3 years while HPC grew from 2% in FY24 to 14% in FY26
items.quote: in FY22 we were 100% into textiles, in FY25 we came down to 85%, and in FY26 we concluded at less than 75%. Going forward, over the next three years, while we will continue to grow in textiles, the textile contribution should come down to below 50% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Business model shifted from white-label to own-brand via distribution partners; adding direct corporate customers; exclusive South Asia partner for Lamoral Coatings with Southeast Asia expansion pending
items.quote: We are exclusive partners for Lamoral for the entire region.

items.statement: Exports 5% of FY26 revenue across 12 countries; Bangladesh ~20% of FY25 exports; targeting South Asia, Southeast Asia, Africa; North America and Europe opportunistic
items.quote: Exports currently account for around 5% of our revenue of FY26 and we believe that this represents a significant long-term opportunity.

items.statement: Trade receivables INR48 cr (~160 days) elevated due to Q4 seasonality (32% of annual revenue); 35%+ of FY26 receivables collected by May; payables down due to MSME mandates and war-related inventory procurement
items.quote: Quarter four itself contributed over 32% of our annual revenue. So the figure that you see in the books, which is around INR48 crores as trade receivables, reflects a weighted average of around 160 days.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings reduced from INR14.3 cr to INR0.7 cr in FY26 using IPO proceeds; debt-to-equity improved from 1.8 to 0.2; short-term borrowings INR17.1 cr for working capital
items.quote: Long-term borrowings were substantially reduced to just INR0.7 crores in FY26 from INR14.3 crores FY25. This reflects our disciplined approach to capital allocation and our decision to utilize a portion of IPO proceeds towards repayment of legacy debt

items.statement: IPO proceeds used for legacy debt repayment; balance sheet significantly strengthened
items.quote: This reflects our disciplined approach to capital allocation and our decision to utilize a portion of IPO proceeds towards repayment of legacy debt

items.statement: R&D spend ~2% of revenue historically and in FY26; targeting 2-3% for current year, then need-based
items.quote: R&D spend was around 2% of our revenue, and broadly FY26 also closed at around 2%. We would like to maintain it in the range of around 2% to 3% for this year.

items.statement: West Asia crisis impact partially hedged via inventory and price pass-through; bio-based esters provide partial crude hedge but logistics/utilities exposed; war continuation could impact projections within +/-10% variance
items.quote: with a plus-minus 10% variance, we still fee l that our numbers and projections should remain intact if the war continues.

items.statement: Employee cost peaked from FY21 strategic hiring; team built before revenue scale; minimal inflationary growth due to attrition balancing additions
items.quote: So we had incurred a significant employee cost from FY21 onwards, wherein the results started becoming visible from FY23. So once you have the team in place, you do not need to keep adding more and more people.

items.statement: MSME payment mandates reduced trade payables days from 117 to 56; Europe REACH compliance a barrier; awaiting FTA clarity for Europe expansion
items.quote: Since the Government of India has MSME payment mandates, naturally we have to clear a significant amount of MSME payments towards the end of the year, and that is one impact.

items.statement: Benefiting from MNC consolidation in textile chemicals; Indian players with right products/services gaining share; Lamoral partnership brings fluorine-free tech as PFAS regulations tighten globally
items.quote: there has been a lot of consolidation in multinational companies, wherein Indian companies that are providin g the right products and right services are getting significant benefits.

items.statement: Broad-based demand across portfolio and end-user industries drove 32% revenue growth; HPC and paints/coatings identified as key growth drivers alongside textiles
items.quote: Revenue from operations for FY26 stood at INR110.7 crores, representing a growth of 32% year -on-year, driven by broad -based demand across our product portfolio and end-user industries.

items.statement: Intends to move to quarterly reporting after H1 FY27 review; currently half-yearly as SME listing
items.quote: We will review it after H1.

items.statement: FY28 and beyond targets not set yet; only FY27 visibility provided
items.quote: Not yet. No, those targets are not set yet. As of now, I cannot even say anything about FY '28. So we can only talk about FY '27 today.

items.statement: Offshore revenue INR75-80 crores yearly, port revenue INR12-15 crores yearly; oil spill response flattening as contracts end
items.value: Offshore INR75-80 crores; Port INR12-15 crores

items.quote: So the raising of preferential was for -- not only for buying new vessels, but also for repayment of our high-cost loans. So we have done that to whatever we have promised. And so up to approximately INR5 crores to INR6 crores, we have already repaid in March 2026

In the port services and oilfield response, it will be about 6.5 years, seven years right

items.statement: Not buying vessels speculatively despite peer expansion; asset prices high due to Gulf crisis; will only purchase with confirmed contracts
items.quote: So we -- as a company, we find that the -- because the market pricing is very high for assets as of today, we do not want to get caught in a high asset value and then get stuck in it because when we buy an asset, we have to buy it for the next 10 to 15 years at least.

items.statement: DG circulars pushing fleet renewal at 20 years vs previous 25 years; electric tug tenders from Mumbai/Kolkata/Chennai ports not commercially viable at current capex
items.quote: So we typically tend to change the fleet after 25 years, but there have been recent DG circulars, which are asking us to basically, the government is asking the owners to renew the fleet at a younger age, say, about 20 years right now.

items.statement: FY26 net profit INR14.72 crores (+25%), EPS INR9.13 (+11.5%), revenue flat INR97.55 crores
items.value: INR14.72 crores PAT; INR97.55 crores revenue
items.quote: Our net profit actually grew by 25% to INR14.72 crores, and our earnings grew by -- earnings per share grew 11.5% to INR9.13. Revenue, however, was broadly flat as compared to last year at INR97.55.

items.statement: JV with UPG Group (26% stake) for shipbuilding/repair/offshore supply base in Odisha; SPV United Sadhav Integrated Maritime formed; land identified, awaiting government allocation
items.quote: We have also formed an SPV joint venture company between the UPG group and Sadhav Shipping Ltd which is named as United Sadhav Integrated Maritime Private Limited, in which Sadhav is a 26% joint venture partner.

items.statement: Electric tug capex too high vs 15-year annuity charter rates; not participating in tenders until economics improve
items.quote: We do not believe that -- or rather we are of the firm belief that the capex for the electric boat is too high as of today. Unless it comes down, the expected charter rate on the annuity basis for 15 years is not making commercial sense.

items.statement: No specific working capital metrics discussed; focus on cost mitigation and confirmed revenue contracts
items.quote: We are also looking at how to mitigate those. Yeah. And then we are also -- the new businesses that are supposed to come in are getting delayed because of this geopolitical crisis actually.

items.statement: Q4 domestic net sales grew 9.2% year-on-year with broad-based growth across Core, Premium, Toothpaste, Toothbrush and Personal Care
items.quote: We have seen over the last quarter a significant acceleration in net sales growth for Q4, our domestic growth now at 9.2%.

items.statement: Q4 gross margin at 69.6% and EBITDA margin a shade over 32%, described as best in class
items.quote: Gross margins continue to be strong at 69.6% and EBITDA margins continue to be absolutely best in class at a shade over 32%.

items.statement: Expect urban markets to continue seeing growth off a soft base; rural to grow faster than urban but not as far ahead as in 2025; overall market flat-to-increasing
items.quote: We do expect that the urban markets will continue to see a little bit of growth coming as they do off a relatively soft base. And we do expect that rural, while it will grow faster than urban, will continue to be maybe not as much ahead as it was through the whole of 2025.

items.statement: Premium portfolio advertising investment stepped up significantly; Colgate Visible White Purple called most successful innovation in Colgate's history; PerioGard franchise doubling year-on-year
items.quote: This has been by far Colgate's most successful innovation in the history of Colgate. An outstanding product which is differentiated and sits in a niche space where 42% of Indians actually want whiter teeth.

items.statement: Reached 1.7 million outlets directly; added 2 lakh stores in 2025; distribution inventory exceptionally well-managed and decreasing
items.quote: We reached 1.7 million outlets directly. We added 2 lakh more stores to our overall reach in 2025.

items.statement: Plants tracked by digital twin for proactive actions and efficiency; AI used to shorten innovation time cycles and improve quality
items.quote: Our plants now get tracked automatically by the digital twin, where there is a twin that runs alongside the main plant and allows us to be proactive in terms of our actions and also make sure that efficiency and throughput remain at the top of the pile.

items.statement: Colgate Strong Teeth clinically proven 8.5x more effective at re-mineralizing than competition
items.quote: Strong Teeth is 8.5x more effective at re-mineralizing, which is really what prevents you from getting cavities and building the strength of your enamel than the competition.

items.statement: GST impact on pricing from September-October 2025 distorted value growth; need to focus on volume growth as MRP pricing has gone down
items.quote: Given the impact of GST on pricing from September-October of last year, we really do need to take a continuous look at volume growth because the value growth pickup that you get in Nielsen will be quite distorted, given that MRP pricing has actually gone down.

items.statement: Core portfolio products 100% superior to competition per consumer testing; Toothbrush value tier leader at 1.7x nearest competitor
items.quote: Our products are now 100% superior to competition across the core, so every single brand has a formulation that is superior to its eyeball competition as decided by consumers, not as decided by technical testing.

items.statement: Rural consumption pilot in Uttar Pradesh moved attitude by ~7%, got 7% delta in brushing once and significant delta in claimed brushing twice
items.quote: What we found out of this is that we are significantly able to move attitude by about 7%, get 7% delta in terms of people brushing once, and a significant delta in terms of claimed brushing twice.

items.statement: Entering Calendar Year 2026 with renewed optimism and confidence in consistent long-term growth delivery
items.quote: As we enter the Calendar Year 2026, we feel a renewed sense of optimism and confidence in terms of what this business can deliver.

items.statement: Harry Potter range for kids launching very soon; Max Fresh Sensorials extended with berry variant; Kids Squeezy and on-the-go mouthwash sticks launched
items.quote: We have a Harry Potter range that's going to hit shelves very, very soon, so this is a sneak peek, not yet available.

items.statement: Distribution inventory continues to be exceptionally well-managed and decreasing as forecasting gets more efficient
items.quote: Distribution inventory continues to be exceptionally well-managed, and we actually keep decreasing it as we get more efficient and as forecasting gets more efficient.

items.statement: Whitening segment growing 4x faster than overall Toothpaste category; 42% of Indians want whiter teeth
items.quote: A category segment that is growing 4x faster than the overall Toothpaste category. The idea of Colgate Visible White Purple is actually very, very simple.

items.quote: The margin performance remains roughly in line with what you are seeing for Q4. And profitability also remains slightly challenged given that the top line growth has been flat.

items.statement: Full year net sales flat; second half grew at shade over 5% vs first half

items.statement: Colgate Max Fresh continues as fastest growing franchise; leveraging blue variant for summer freshness delivery

items.statement: GST provided opportunity to launch Rs. 10 toothbrush at lower entry price point
items.quote: GST provided us a real opportunity to make sure that we could do the Rs. 10 brush, and we have capitalized on it.

items.statement: Urban consumer replaces toothbrush once in 6 months; rural consumer as slowly as once in 15 months; new brush cleans 95% better than old
items.quote: On average, the urban consumer replaces his or her Toothbrush once in six months. Rural consumers replace their Toothbrush as slowly as once in 15 months. And a new Toothbrush cleans 95% better than an old, frayed, flared Toothbrush.

items.statement: Module capacity expanding from 2.4 GW to 3.6 GW

items.quote: currently 1 megawatt of T OPCon solar cell is selling around Rs.13 to Rs.14, so that means 1 GW will get us Rs.1,350 crore s kind of revenue from only the cell from 1 GW.

items.quote: we have maintained a large inventory, if you would have seen in our balance sheet numbers also. So, we are sitting on an inventory of Rs.316 crores, which is quite adequate to handle the pressures of vagaries and some challenges.

items.statement: 80-85% of 2.2 GW cell output for captive use; ~20% barter/sold for other sizes (M10R vs G12R)
items.quote: Look, our capacity is 2.2 GW and 80% to 85% we intend to use in-house and maybe 20 % we will be again doing a kind of a barter because we have requirements for the other sizes from the market.

items.statement: Customer base includes PSUs and private entities (e.g., Luminous, NPCL); DCR and non-DCR sales mix varies quarterly
items.quote: We deal with a variety of customers including PSUs as well as private entities, so, we have customers like Luminous Starter, NPCL and many more.

In a normal case, one would wait, do tendering, bring another vessel and the appraisal process would have happened 1-year or 2-year down the line. We renegotiated the contract and got the seismic vessel to mobilize the spread on an ASAP basis and carry out the seismic data acquisition for our appraisal process.

items.statement: Released drillable location inventory increased from ~45 to 218; average well depth increased from 2,300-2,500m to 4,300m; 100 wells/year target sustained by two-tier scrutiny mechanism

And we have our internal mechanism, a two-tier scrutiny mechanism to release these locations. So, to our mind, the Assam shelf, while we were doing an average depth of 2,300 to 2,500 meters three years ago, last year we did an average depth of 4,300 meters.

items.statement: Indo-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline exporting HSD continues despite Bangladesh turmoil; not sole pivot for 9 MMT viability
